    4 random apps you might not realize work with Android Auto

    📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1331 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Engadget

    ⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Some of these apps will be familiar, while others you may not have heard of.
    • Recent findings suggest that android Auto consumers typically utilize just a few basic apps like Google Maps for directions and Spotify for music.
    • In a recent development, android Auto actually supports a surprising range of communication and meeting tools, like WhatsApp and Google Meet, and even a bunch of other apps to help you navigate more efficiently.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Some of these apps will be familiar, while others you may not have heard of.

    Recent findings suggest that android Auto consumers typically utilize just a few basic apps like Google Maps for directions and Spotify for music. They don't dive into the developer menu; they don't make any serious changes to the way Android Auto works; and they don't know they could be spending all those minutes waiting for someone in a parking lot playing games directly on the car's infotainment display. But the platform's compatible app library runs much deeper, well beyond navigation and streaming.

    In a recent development, android Auto actually supports a surprising range of communication and meeting tools, like WhatsApp and Google Meet, and even a bunch of other apps to help you navigate more efficiently. Each one adds layer after layer of functionality that most customers never think to explore. Discovering new apps can genuinely change how you commute while also making it possible to enjoy your drive just a tiny bit more.

    Android Auto comes with some extra functionality for those in the corporate world, as several popular apps come with Android Auto support for meetings and calls, with Google Meet leading the way. Because Meet is Google's own app, it fits naturally into the Android Auto experience. You can see your upcoming meetings on the car display and join a call with a single tap, all in audio-only mode so your eyes stay on the road. Whether it's a short check-in with your manager or a longer team call, Meet makes it easy to keep up with your schedule even if you have to drive around.

    It has been revealed that google's app isn't the only option, though. Zoom, Webex by Cisco and Microsoft Teams all work on Android Auto, offering users the opportunity to join video conferences with audio only. Some apps take integration a step further. Microsoft Teams, for instance, lets users check their calendar and place calls directly from the car display. Google Meet also displays upcoming meetings on your schedule. These features are particularly useful if you're often traveling from location to location but still have to participate in meetings along the way. They also help if you have to leave early to pick up the kids from school while a meeting is still on your calendar.

    According to recent reports, one thing to mention about these apps is that, depending on your employer, restrictions may apply. Certain companies require corporate apps like Google Meet and Microsoft Teams to run inside an isolated Android Work Profile. In such situations, Android Auto may block calendar sync or prevent the app from appearing on the screen. There's a Work Mode in the works on Android Auto, though, so it may soon be easier to reach all those apps that are locked out by your employer.

    It has been revealed that with gas prices being what they are these days, it's more vital than ever to know where to fuel up. Apps like Fuelio can help with that when you're looking for a place to put gas in your car without breaking the bank. Fuelio tracks fill-ups, odometer readings and fuel prices, then calculates your average fuel economy and cost per mile over time. You can even use various filters to display gas stations that were updated within the past day, or those that are most appreciated by users.

    Industry observers note that google Maps and other similar tools can surface the nearest gas stations and even tell you the latest prices, but Fuelio gives more in-depth information regarding fuel type, distance and more. Plus, when you throw in all the other features, it's a much better fit if you want to know exactly how much your car is costing you. While Fuelio is free to use with Android Auto, there is a premium version available that costs money.

    According to recent reports, if you're driving an EV, then the app you absolutely must use through Android Auto is PlugShare. This free tool (the paid version removes ads) gives you access to a crowd-sourced map that lets you see the nearest charging stations along your route. Its real strength is the community behind it, because drivers leave real-time feedback, uploading photos of the charger layout, reporting broken plugs and checking in after charging. That gives you a clear picture of what to expect before you pull in, so a station that looks fine on paper but has been out of service for days won't catch you off guard.

    In a recent development, there are loads of filters you can play with, letting you choose the exact plug type, charging speed and network. You can also check which amenities are nearby, such as restrooms or a place to grab coffee while you wait. It's also a great tool for long-distance drives, as it automatically recommends charging stops along the way based on your specific EV model's range. That goes a long way toward easing the range anxiety that comes with getting an electric car. The one downside is that the data is only as good as its contributors, so stations in less-traveled areas may have fewer recent reports.

    Data can be expensive, especially if you use your phone a ton. When you're traveling abroad, costs go up by quite a bit, so you should make the most of your home Wi-Fi. Apps like HERE WeGo through Android Auto offer offline navigation, so your data strategy isn't ever a concern. HERE WeGo lets you download maps for entire countries so you always know where you're going. For some countries, you can download maps for certain areas, such as for Germany where you can grab a map for Berlin and another for Hamburg. In the United States, you can grab maps for entire states, but not separate cities.

    It has been revealed that there are plenty of features to fiddle with to make this app yours, like choosing which fuel type your car uses, having the metric vs. imperial system displayed the way you prefer and so on. The app will flag parking spots and rest areas along the route, and you can even tell it what types of things to avoid. For instance, Waze lets you avoid ferries and highways, but HERE WeGo can have you avoid tunnels and U-turns too. The app can take things one step further and even use visual references on route, which means it will tell you to make a right at the traffic light or when you reach a certain landmark.

    Sources indicate that yes, Android Auto will read out your texts — we all know that. But it can also handle other apps, reading out your messages if you so desire and then letting you use your voice to reply. WhatsApp is the clearest example of this working well, as Android Auto can read your messages aloud. Then, Gemini asks if you want to reply and will type out the words for you. Signal offers similar read-aloud and reply functionality; so do Facebook Messenger, Microsoft Teams and Google Chat, to name a few.

    This feature can be super useful when you're driving as you can stay connected without taking your eyes off the road. The ability to reply to messages will also help you stay on top of any emergencies without having to pull over. However, as with any AI typing tool, you should expect some mistakes here and there.

    Industry observers note that adding all these apps is straightforward as you only have to install them from the Google Play Store on your phone. Compatible apps will automatically pop up on your Android Auto launcher. You can go into the Android Auto settings and reorganize the apps if you want to make some more easily accessible. Android Auto's compatibility list is wider than most people assume, but the best setup prioritizes the tools that you actually use when you're behind the wheel.

    Trafalgar Square Christmas tree felled in Norway

    📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (449 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Co

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Karen Scarborough (left) and Anne Lindboe got to work with a two-handled saw.
    • This year's Trafalgar Square Christmas tree has been cut down in a forest outside Oslo, ready to begin its journey to London.
    • The 21m (69ft) tree, nicknamed Jolly Cheery, is about 75 years old.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Karen Scarborough (left) and Anne Lindboe got to work with a two-handled saw.

    This year's Trafalgar Square Christmas tree has been cut down in a forest outside Oslo, ready to begin its journey to London.

    The 21m (69ft) tree, nicknamed Jolly Cheery, is about 75 years old. It was felled on Friday by the Lord Mayor of Westminster, Karen Scarborough, and the Mayor of Oslo, Anne Lindboe.

    Norway has sent a tree to the capital every year since 1947 as a thank you for Britain's support during World War Two, when King Haakon VII and the Norwegian government lived in exile in London.

    Its lights will be switched on by the two mayors at a ceremony in the square on Thursday, 3 December.

    Scarborough remarked: "It's my greatest honour to take part in this wonderful tradition for both the cities of Oslo and London.

    "This tree is a powerful symbol of friendship and peace, reminding us to be there for one another during the festive period.".

    The 21m tree has been nicknamed Jolly Cheery.

    Scarborough thanked "the people of Oslo and Norway for this truly fabulous gift" and added: "With the care and dedication of the team, I'm sure it will look magnificent on Trafalgar Square.".

    Lindboe remarked: "Oslo has been sending a Christmas tree to London for almost eight decades, and every year we send a tree across the North Sea with the same message: we have not forgotten.

    "The tradition has a powerful history, and its message remains just as relevant today.

    "I hope Jolly Cheery spreads warmth and Christmas cheer to everyone who passes by, and reminds us how much it means to be there for one another, especially in difficult times.".

    Count the rings: Anne Lindboe (left) and Karen Scarborough (right) with a slice of the 75-year-old trunk.

    For the second year running, the tree was chosen with the help of a social media poll.

    Industry observers note that organisers said it would travel by road in Norway and England using only electric and biodiesel vehicles, cutting the journey's carbon footprint by 80%. It will cross the North Sea on a regular cargo ship from the port of Brevik.

    Once in London, it will be decorated in the traditional Norwegian style, with 25m strings of festoon lighting fitted with energy-efficient bulbs.

    It has been revealed that earlier this week at the DealBook conference in Fresh York, Elon Musk, beamed in from a trip to China with President Donald Trump, was asked about the ouster of his longtime friend, former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. Musk compared it to kicking Michael Jordan off the Chicago Bulls’ roster during his historic run. Of Nvidia’s employees, he remarked, “They love [Huang]. They love him.”.

    Industry observers note that well, maybe not all of them. Thousands of employees have signed a letter asking for Huang’s return, but others tell The New York Times he ruled through praise and fear, as well as by humiliating people.

    According to recent reports, according to the Times, Huang told subordinates that Nvidia’s wealth meant it wasn’t possible to motivate employees with money, so humiliation was the only lever left. He reportedly told one executive his mother should have aborted him and told another employee he would rip his arms off and beat him to death with them.

    Sources indicate that naturally, over a 33-year career, regrettable things may have been remarked, but the Times found a long paper trail that suggests the incidents weren’t isolated. In 2005, for example, Michael Winston, a former HR chief, threatened to sue and called Huang’s conduct the most abusive he’d seen. Nvidia paid him more than $1 million. Huang’s spokesman calls the allegations fabrications.

    #58833. Amazon fights the Delivery Protection Act with homepage banner, in-app pop-up

    📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (537 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Ars Technica ↗ Open Full Page

    Amazon fights the Delivery Protection Act with homepage banner, in-app pop-up

    📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (537 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Ars Technica

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In an unprecedented move, Amazon is using its app and website to try to convince shoppers to not support a Latest York City bill.
    • Industry observers note that I also saw a smaller version of the notice on an order confirmation page on Amazon’s website.
    • It has been revealed that amazon is referring to Introduction 0518-2026 ( 518), also known as the Delivery Protection Act.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In an unprecedented move, Amazon is using its app and website to try to convince shoppers to not support a Latest York City bill.

    Industry observers note that I also saw a smaller version of the notice on an order confirmation page on Amazon’s website. The message is delivered as a pop-up for users of the Amazon app, Bloomberg reported. Amazon hasn’t specified whether the messaging targets NYC residents based on addresses saved in their Amazon account or uses other techniques, such as device location services, but I only see the banner if I’m logged in to Amazon.

    It has been revealed that amazon is referring to Introduction 0518-2026 ( 518), also known as the Delivery Protection Act. If passed, it would require Amazon to directly employ the third-party delivery contractors that it uses.

    Clicking on “Act now” on Amazon’s homepage or in the app brings up a page that gives shoppers a way to contact their NYC Council member and further states:.

    According to recent reports, right now, Amazon works with a network of small delivery businesses that are deeply embedded in your communities. If this legislation passes, we’d no longer be able to work with them, and we’d be forced to consider moving our operations outside of the city. That would likely mean slower and more expensive delivery for millions of customers in New York City, while also threatening small businesses and their thousands of employees.

    According to recent reports, it’s not unusual for Amazon to take a stance on political matters, and it has publicly opposed the Delivery Protection Act since April. What is newly introduced is Amazon using its online marketplace to push a political view. It’s uncommon to see a pop-up about legislation when visiting a shopping website.

    The messaging suggests that Amazon is concerned about the potential impact the proposed law would have on its costs. Besides Amazon, the bill targets any company with last-mile delivery facilities in NYC, like FedEx and DoorDash.

    It also raises questions about the potential impact on shoppers should Amazon expand its use of its e-commerce platform for additional political messaging. The pop-up launched today impacts only NYC residents but sets a precedent for Amazon to sway political views on other issues. Amazon has made similar moves internally, including reportedly using an app for its employees to campaign against unionizing. But the new pop-up highlights Amazon extending that strategy directly to its users.

    Industry observers note that given Amazon’s considerable influence in commerce, other companies could copy its actions. Uber and Lyft have previously done so, CNBC reports.

    Finally, there’s the question of whether Amazon is fairly depicting the situations surrounding the bill. Notable supporters of the Delivery Protection Act include NYC Mayor Zohran Mamdani and the Amazon division of the International Brotherhood of Teamsters. Using a platform with massive reach to communicate only one side of an ongoing debate could lead to misinformation and a skewed public perception.

    The Delivery Protection Act is presently stalled in the City Council’s Committee on Consumer and Worker Protection. The last hearing on the bill was in April. A committee vote on whether to advance the act to the full City Council hasn’t been set.

    Breaking: Inspired by Bernie Sanders: A German agency is using US-Style campaigning to boost the left in 2029

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • According to recent reports, red, red, green — those are the party colors of the left-leaning coalition recently formed in the German state of Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania.
    • The Goodforces wants to help make that a reality with their campaign neunund20 (twenty-nine), taking its cue, in part, from the American left.
    • Co-founder Patrick Haermeyer told DW that the campaign's aim is "to give people hope and an alternative narrative to: Things are getting worse and worse." He worked as an online organizer for the election team of Bernie Sanders in the US Democratic presidential primaries in 2016 and cites Sanders' "not me, us" campaign as an inspiration.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, red, red, green — those are the party colors of the left-leaning coalition recently formed in the German state of Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania. Now a Berlin-based agency wants to see the same alliance between the center-left Social Democrats, the socialist Left Party, and environmentalist Greens win the 2029 national elections.

    The Goodforces wants to help make that a reality with their campaign neunund20 (twenty-nine), taking its cue, in part, from the American left. The agency was set up in response to the rise of the far right across Europe.

    Co-founder Patrick Haermeyer told DW that the campaign's aim is "to give people hope and an alternative narrative to: Things are getting worse and worse." He worked as an online organizer for the election team of Bernie Sanders in the US Democratic presidential primaries in 2016 and cites Sanders' "not me, us" campaign as an inspiration.

    Industry observers note that neunund20 currently has two strategies: It provides digital space for short-form videos and social media content on political and social topics on Instagram, Tiktok, and Bluesky. At the same time, it tries to connect content creators, activists, NGOs, and political initiatives around shared "progressive" challenges.

    Recent findings suggest that users with a particular interest can click to get a link giving them access to archives of relevant social media material that they can then reshare. That feature is modelled on the campaign of Newly introduced York's left-wing mayor Zohran Mamdani.

    And there are other projects. The Goodforces was recently involved in a tactical voting initiative in the September elections in the state of Saxony-Anhalt, intended to keep the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) from winning an absolute majority. Haermeyer notes physical campaigns of that kind are necessary to provide essential "interim victories" en route to the next parliamentary elections.

    Sources indicate that the Greens and the SPD, the two parties recommended by the app created by the organization, made it over the 5% hurdle and into parliament. The help that they received was declared by each party in the form of a €40,000 ($43,900) donation.

    To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

    The agency sees itself as a kind of Super PAC, modeled on political organizations in the United States that collect money to carry out campaigns without directly supporting a single party or a special candidate.

    For Christoph Bieber, political scientist at the University of Duisburg-Essen, the Goodforces is an interesting newly introduced type of player on Germany's political scene because it operates outside the country's political parties.

    Sources indicate that but many of those parties are eyeing the development with disquiet. The far-left, populist, immigration skeptical Alliance for Social Justice and Economic Reason (BSW) criticized the Goodforces' intervention in Saxony-Anhalt, telling the newspaper FAZ that it was an "infantilizing, and perhaps even antidemocratic action." The neoliberal Free Democrats (FDP) called the tool "wrong and intentionally misleading." The FDP failed to clear the threshold, while the BSW only just squeaked in. The AfD gained 43% of the vote and its candidate may soon become Germany's first far-right state premier since the Nazi era.

    To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

    Sources indicate that haermeyer set up the agency in 2024 along with Peter Jelinek, and both men previously worked for Green Party European Parliament member Michael Bloss. Ahead of that year's European elections, the EU's Green Deal began to come under increasing attack.

    That year also ended with the collapse of Germany's first federal coalition between the SPD, Greens, and FDP, after much infighting and attacks from right-wing quarters.

    According to recent reports, "We noticed that more and more successes and freedoms that we had fought for were being reversed: Things like freedom of movement, border checks, and other things that were coming more and more under fire," Haermeyer told DW. "And we noticed that it was primarily democratic and progressive forces that were being drawn into defensive battles.".

    It has been revealed that the AfD, founded in 2013, already in the age of social media, has successfully targeted younger voters with in its online campaigns. But the older parties, in particular, have struggled. The Goodforces saw a need for support in the online environment and is now seeking to plug this gap.

    Recent findings suggest that the social media accounts of the campaign neunund20 contain posts on domestic German topics, such as the current negotiations to form a red-red-green coalition government in Berlin, and the country's latest military service law. They also highlight "wins" in Spain in the protests for affordable housing and for US Democrats in the midterms.

    Haermeyer stresses that the issues the agency highlights are determined together with a wide range of grassroots organizations and activists. "The campaign is not agreed in conjunction with the SPD, the Left Party, and the Greens," he noted.

    Agency funding comes from commissions and small donations. Haermeyer says that contributions generally range from $20 to $50.

    To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

    Bieber sees the emergence of non-party campaigning, long an accepted practice in the US, as a bid to compensate for the shortcomings of traditional parties.

    Sources indicate that "It is an omission of the parties," he said. "For years they have been saying we have to modernize, we have to become more open and get away from rigid membership structures. There are legal regulations governing the organization of political parties in Germany, but perhaps it could be more flexible and open.".

    Recent findings suggest that the center-left and center-right major-tent parties have been in decline for decades. Membership of the SPD dropped from 943,000 in 1990 to some 348,000 at the end of 2025. Chancellor Friedrich Merz's Christian Democratic Union (CDU) has seen a fall from 750,000 to under 357,000.

    Recent findings suggest that party membership is particularly low in former communist eastern Germany. Centrist parties have also struggled to attract younger voters. A report by the Deutsche Kinder und Jugendstiftung (German Children and Youth Foundation) indicated that only 20% of young people felt their concerns were taken seriously in the 2025 German elections and that trust in parties was low.

    Sources indicate that in the United States, campaign financing comes predominantly from donations, and lobby groups can buy influence by contributing unlimited amounts to super PACs. In Germany, party funding comes, in part, from taxpayers and membership fees, and donations are capped. However, Bieber warns that whereas there are strict rules regarding the disclosure of donors to US Super PACs, these do not exist in Germany.

    In a recent development, the political scientist does not believe that US-style campaigning is going to take hold in Germany, but he does see potential dangers: "This could be a door opener to make others consider whether they want to go in this direction in the field of campaigning. And he added: "If it becomes rife, it could lead to a further devaluation of parties and their structures.".

    Fixing this annoying One UI feature is easy, but there's a catch

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Moving the Now bar back down to the bottom of your lock screen is easy.
    • According to recent reports, one UI is packed with features that set Samsung's phones apart from any other Android phones — for better or worse, depending on who you ask.
    • The Now bar is nothing newly introduced.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Moving the Now bar back down to the bottom of your lock screen is easy.

    According to recent reports, one UI is packed with features that set Samsung's phones apart from any other Android phones — for better or worse, depending on who you ask. Even if you don't know it by name, you've probably used the Now bar if you have a Samsung phone. It's the little capsule that shows up on the lock screen, showing timers, notes, news updates or media player controls based on which apps you've allowed to appear there.

    The Now bar is nothing newly introduced. It was introduced in One UI 7 and has been tweaked in updates since then. But if you've switched phones or adjusted your settings, you may notice that the Now bar hovers around the middle third of your screen instead of at the very bottom where it does by default on some phones. In some lock screen setups, the higher location of the Now bar can cover other widgets, making them harder to read or tap. Many users also just prefer the look of the Now bar sitting at the very bottom. There are a couple of ways to make sure your Now bar stays along the phone's bottom edge, but they both require sacrificing one of your phone's lock screen features.

    Industry observers note that fingerprint readers can appear in different places on your phone, depending on the model. The problem arises in phones with a fingerprint reader at the bottom of the screen. While the Now bar is usually along the bottom edge of the phone's screen, that overlaps with where the fingerprint reader sits. While you can typically customize your phone's look with One UI, the operating system automatically pushes the Now bar up above the fingerprint reader when both are turned on so they don't overlap. Unfortunately, there's no way to reposition either feature.

    It has been revealed that to move your Now bar back to the bottom of the screen, you need to turn your fingerprint reader off entirely. To do that, head to the Settings app and tap Security and privacy, then Screen lock and biometrics. Here you can delete any fingerprints you have stored and remove the fingerprint reader as your unlock option. If you don't want to leave your phone unlocked, there are other options, like setting a password or face recognition, that will still help keep your phone secure but won't interfere with the Now bar.

    Sources indicate that if you can't go without the fingerprint reader and don't use lock screen notifications much, you may just want to turn the Now bar off. Back in the Settings app, tap Lock screen, then Now bar. Here you can toggle which apps have access to the Now bar individually. If you turn them all off, you'll never see the Now bar. However, the Now bar is the only way to keep media controls on the lock screen, so you may want to keep the media player switched on while turning everything else off. That way, you'll still see the media controls when you need them.

    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Theguardian ↗ Open Full Page

    Potty-mouthed MPs ranked as Australian parliament sets fresh swearing record

    📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1098 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Theguardian

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • One serial swearing offender, Jacqui Lambie, states it wouldn’t be an Australian parliament ‘without a few swear words thrown in’.
    • When Liberal MP Garth Hamilton stormed out of parliament in June, slamming his hands on his desk and calling out “fucking bullshit”, the speaker of the house, Milton Dick, called it “a new low” in federal politics.
    • Fresh analysis from Guardian Australia has found profanity and foul language has risen significantly in Australia’s parliament over the past 20 years, with some of today’s most prominent politicians among the chief culprits for swearing.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    One serial swearing offender, Jacqui Lambie, states it wouldn’t be an Australian parliament ‘without a few swear words thrown in’.

    When Liberal MP Garth Hamilton stormed out of parliament in June, slamming his hands on his desk and calling out “fucking bullshit”, the speaker of the house, Milton Dick, called it “a new low” in federal politics.

    Dick may have been on to something.

    Fresh analysis from Guardian Australia has found profanity and foul language has risen significantly in Australia’s parliament over the past 20 years, with some of today’s most prominent politicians among the chief culprits for swearing.

    In a recent development, before the year is even out, 2026 is the worst year on record for the use of swear words and language deemed “unparliamentary”. That number has risen by 78% since 2006.

    Analysis of Hansard debate and procedure records has found that per million words spoken in parliament this year, approximately 37 have been profane – ranging from milder (“bloody”, “damn” and “crap”) to language considered strong, or even extreme.

    While entitled to “parle hard”, language deemed unparliamentary by the speaker or Senate president is required to be withdrawn, or else MPs face ejection from the chamber.

    Beyond the impact of pushing against regulation and etiquette, there is something to be noted for the currency that outbursts gain when clipped and shared online – recently demonstrated by Greens senator Peter Whish-Wilson, who called for the country to “wake the fuck up” to One Nation’s use of social media algorithms in June.

    But despite the politicians reaching for profanities at a record rate, Dick – the Labor MP who has been speaker of the house since 2022 – remarked he felt the tone and tenor of debate in parliament has got better in his time in the chair.

    “Debate is fierce and strong and, apart from a few incidents, it has improved,” he noted.

    “Maybe it hasn’t appeared so because of the volume [of swearing], but when you analyse the words used … there are outbreaks of course, but I believe in everyone showing respect.”.

    And, to be fair, most of parliament’s most swear-y politicians are in the Senate, not the house.

    According to recent reports, described as “the great Australian adjective” in 1894 by the Bulletin magazine, “bloody” appears to have suffered no fall from grace in the subsequent years, serving as the most commonly used swear word in parliament. Along with “damn”, “crap” and “bugger”, mild curses constitute 92% of all recorded bad language, with more severe terms such as “prick”, “shit” and “piss” used more sparingly.

    Excluded from this figure are rare cases of colourful and creative terms that have been called for withdrawal. Harnessing the speaker’s unilateral power to flag unacceptable language, terms such as “bin chickens – used by Julian Hill, the MP for Bruce, in 2022 to describe the opposition in the house – have been ruled as unparliamentary.

    Much of this potty-talk comes from the Senate, which since 2006 has seen a 177% increase in the use of bad language. Among active parliamentary participants (those who have spoken at least 100,000 words in this period), Bill Heffernan was the lead offender. Despite speaking just 141,000 words between 2006 and 2016, the former Liberal senator had an expletive use-rate of 877 per million words spoken, 43 times the rate of all other parliamentarians.

    Recent findings suggest that jacqui Lambie is the second-most sweary politician, responsible for 6% of total swearing in parliament at a rate of 406 per million words spoken – more than 19 times the average. But, like most of the politicians on this list, Lambie’s swearing is overwhelmingly mild – mostly words like “crap” or “bloody”.

    “I try really hard not to swear, especially in the Senate chamber. It upsets my mum, she doesn’t even like me saying ‘bloody’,” Lambie stated when we came to her with the statistics.

    “It’s important to be respectful. But I am a straight shooter and sometimes things are just crap – and it’s hard not to say so. I don’t think it would be an Australian parliament without a few swear words thrown in.”.

    Recent findings suggest that not all occurrences of swearing in parliamentary records are “own-use” or, rather, swearing with intent. Quotes, such as reading out abuse a politician has received, or a quote from a document, account for some of it.

    However, when excluding these cases our analysis reveals that own-use swearing in parliament has nearly tripled over the last 20 years, from 6.4 per million words in 2006-9 to 18.9 in 2022-5.

    Broken down by party, One Nation are the worst offenders, swearing for the sake of it at 7.4 times the rate of Labor – perhaps unsurprising, given that the party leader, Pauline Hanson, ranks fourth among discursively active politicians for use of foul language.

    Dick said he had strived to improve the tone of discussion in parliament, believing that greater diversity in politics and in the chamber – with more women, more First Nations MPs and people from multicultural backgrounds – had also changed dynamics of debate.

    Asked about recent heated moments in parliament, he remarked he recalled only two major moments in the lower house in recent years Hamilton’s June storm-out and fellow Liberal MP Dan Tehan’s demand to “cut the crap” in August.

    “I want to ensure, among our people and our democracy, that we fight hard to disagree more civilly … But I’m a major believer in upholding traditions and standards. When things get a bit heated, I’ll take firm action,” Dick remarked.

    Sources indicate that politicians’ speeches from both houses of parliament were analysed for the years 2006 to 2026. For each speech, the number of swearwords were counted using the these categories:.

    Mild: bloody, damn, crap, bugger, bastard, bulldust, arse, mongrel, boofhead, bollocks.

    Strong: prick, shit, bullshit, piss, piss off, dickhead, arsehole, shithouse, wanker.

    Extreme: fucking, cunt, fuck, fuck off, fucker, fucked, motherfucker.

    To control for politicians’ tenure length and verbosity affecting swearing totals, swearing numbers were converted to a rate per million words by dividing the total swearwords by the total number of words spoken for that politician in that year, or for the total time period.

    To separate swearing in a politician’s own voice from quotes, idioms and literal uses, an LLM was used to read the speech text surrounding each swearword and sort these into categories. A random sample of the results were manually checked, to achieve an agreement of 97% on whether a use was the speaker’s own. Therefore these figures are approximate.

    It has been revealed that the companion app handles transcription and uses AI to turn recordings into more organized notes and summaries. Customers also get 300 minutes of free audio transcription each month.

    If you need more recording capacity or access to additional AI features, Anker offers optional subscription aims, including Pro ($99 per year) and Unlimited ($239 per year).

    Industry observers note that logitech’s MX Keypad brings AI shortcuts directly to your desk, with dedicated buttons that let you launch your preferred AI assistant or trigger specific productivity tools with a single press. If you frequently switch between different apps and AI assistants, having these shortcuts within reach could make your workday easier.

    The keypad can be configured to work with tools such as GitHub Copilot and Claude Code, along with a range of popular productivity and creative apps, such as OpenAI Codex, Microsoft Teams, PowerPoint, Excel, Notion, Slack, Photoshop, Final Cut Pro, Zoom, and Figma.

    Amazon’s Kindle Scribe Colorsoft brings color to the company’s digital notetaking lineup and offers some neat AI features designed to clean up your messy notes.

    Industry observers note that starting at $479, the device is aimed at people who regularly work with digital documents, including students, researchers, and professionals who prefer annotating files rather than printing them out. It lets you highlight important passages, mark up documents, organize handwritten notes, and sketch out ideas.

    Recent findings suggest that notably, the Scribe Colorsoft incorporates AI-powered tools to clean up messy handwriting, straighten highlighting and underlining, summarize notes, and help turn scattered thoughts into more organized information. Its search feature can look across your saved notes to find specific details and help identify connections between different entries.

    If you’re tired of adjusting your webcam during video calls, Insta360’s Link 2 Pro aims to take care of that for you.

    It has been revealed that priced at $249 (discounted to $199 for Black Friday), this AI-powered webcam combines 4K video capture with intelligent tracking and automatic framing. Its smart video tracker can follow your movements and adjust the camera’s position to keep you in view, even when you move around your workspace, which is particularly useful for people who regularly give presentations, teach online, or switch between sitting at their desk and standing during video calls.

    The camera also offers group tracking, which can come in handy during team meetings or presentations involving multiple people. AI-powered noise cancellation is another useful addition, helping reduce distracting background sounds during calls.

    According to recent reports, your desk could probably use a little intelligence, too. Autonomous Desk Pro is an adjustable standing desk designed to encourage healthier habits throughout the workday.

    Recent findings suggest that beyond switching between sitting and standing positions, the AI-powered desk uses built-in sensors to monitor your activity and remind you when it’s time to move, stretch, or change positions. It can track how much time you spend sitting versus standing, giving you a better idea of your daily work habits.

    The AI features go a step further by allowing you to ask questions about your activity. For example, you can check how long you’ve been sitting, compare your activity with the previous day, or get information about the room’s CO2 levels to help determine whether it’s time to open a window.

    #58825. Here's how to properly test your USB speed

    📅 22 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (791 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Engadget ↗ Open Full Page

    Here's how to properly test your USB speed

    📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (791 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Engadget

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Sources indicate that the USB spec lies at the heart of our computing world, and we're all stuck with the ports, cables, and accessories to prove it.
    • It has been revealed that crystalDiskMark and AmorphousDiskMark for Windows and macOS, respectively, are popular open-source programs for checking storage drives' read and write speeds, but they can also serve as a proxy for determining if your USB connections are running to their intended spec.
    • Sources indicate that windows owners can also confirm whether their connected device is running at the port's top supported speed by installing the Windows SDK and opening up a tool called USBView.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Know whether you're getting what you paid for.

    Sources indicate that the USB spec lies at the heart of our computing world, and we're all stuck with the ports, cables, and accessories to prove it. We pay good money for storage drives and USB hubs with rapid read and write speeds, but the ports we connect them to are just as crucial. You should know if you're getting your money's worth here, and there are programs you can use to diagnose those rates.

    It has been revealed that crystalDiskMark and AmorphousDiskMark for Windows and macOS, respectively, are popular open-source programs for checking storage drives' read and write speeds, but they can also serve as a proxy for determining if your USB connections are running to their intended spec. Connect a drive, open either program, and select it via the drop-down menu. Hitting the first button below All will initiate a sequential read and write test that should give you a good indication of how fast your USB port is. You can then take those transfer rates and see how they compare to what the port (or device) should be capable of.

    Sources indicate that windows owners can also confirm whether their connected device is running at the port's top supported speed by installing the Windows SDK and opening up a tool called USBView. You can access the tool by heading to Program Files (x86) > Windows Kits > 10 > Debuggers. Pick the folder for your machine's architecture, then open USBView. Select your storage device listed in the left pane and look under the Device Information header next to Device Bus Speed. You won't see a version number there, though, but a somewhat wordy descriptor like SuperSpeed 20. More on that later.

    Recent findings suggest that when diagnosing a USB port, use a device (and cable) that meets or exceeds the USB port's capabilities so you can see just how fast the port is. Avoid using a thumb drive, as its performance degrades more quickly during intensive testing. If you're testing a USB hub, connect the hub to the fastest USB port available to eliminate the host computer as the bottleneck.

    You may see USB ports with colored shielding to indicate their speed, but these color schemes aren't universal. You can't also rely on the port itself to determine speed, as USB-C doesn't guarantee high speeds. Instead, you should consult your user manual to see which ports are which. Lacking that, USBView is a great tool for figuring out which port has the latest version, but you'll need to translate the long-form name of a USB version into actual version and transfer rate numbers.

    Storage diagnostic tools will typically present the results in bytes per second, while the USB spec uses bits per second. One byte consists of eight bits, so be prepared to multiply by eight a few times if you want to audit the on-paper capabilities of several ports. Note that data transfers will rarely hit the maximum theoretical speed, but should still exceed the previous USB version. A USB 3.2 Gen 2 device, for example, may not manage 10 Gbps, but it should still beat the 5 Gbps threshold of 3.2 Gen 1.

    The contemporary floor for many modern low-spec devices is USB 2.0 (Hi-Speed, 480 Mbps). Then we get to the different versions of USB 3.2, some previously labeled 3.0 and 3.1: USB 3.2 Gen 1 (SuperSpeed, 5 Gbps), 3.2 Gen 2 (SuperSpeed+, 10 Gbps) and 3.2 Gen 2x2 (SuperSpeed 20, 20 Gbps). USB 4 comes in three speeds: 20 Gbps, 40 Gbps and 80 Gbps (the latter is technically from USB4 version 2). USB 3.2 Gen 2x2 and USB 4 are exclusive to the Type-C connector, while all others support both Type-C and Type-A. If you're using USBView, these are the names and speeds you'll see listed for each USB port.

    Note that USB features backwards compatibility with previous versions, so you're able to get the top speeds allowed for by, say, a USB 2.0 device on a USB4 port. While it is an edge case, it should be noted that the USB 4 spec does not require host devices to support 20Gbps speeds via USB 3.2 Gen 2x2 — some devices do, but otherwise, expect that connection to fall back to 10Gbps on USB 3.2 Gen 2.

    Intel's Thunderbolt shares the Type-C connector and, while there are differences, its transfer speeds map to USB4: Thunderbolt 3 and Thunderbolt 4 were rated for 40 Gbps, while Thunderbolt 5 can hit 80 Gbps in both directions or, with the on-demand Bandwidth Boost feature, split at 40 and 120 Gbps. Make sure you have cables that specifically support the Thunderbolt standard you're looking for.

    Mamdani unveils initiative to close New York's Rikers Island jail by 2032

    📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (713 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Perched on a 413 acre (167 hectare) island between Queens and the Bronx, the notorious Rikers Island jail complex earned a variety of nicknames over the years.
    • Fresh York City's official overseeing the closure of the city's most notorious jail hopes a new strategy from Mayor Zohran Mamdani will lead to "a moment of transformation" for how people are detained in the largest US city.
    • Mamdani on Friday unveiled a plan to close the Rikers Island complex by 2032, to build four new jails and drastically reduce the city's detainee population.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Perched on a 413 acre (167 hectare) island between Queens and the Bronx, the notorious Rikers Island jail complex earned a variety of nicknames over the years.

    Fresh York City's official overseeing the closure of the city's most notorious jail hopes a new strategy from Mayor Zohran Mamdani will lead to "a moment of transformation" for how people are detained in the largest US city.

    Mamdani on Friday unveiled a plan to close the Rikers Island complex by 2032, to build four new jails and drastically reduce the city's detainee population.

    In a recent development, plans to shutter the troubled facility date back to 2019, when the city council first voted to close it by this year. But plans have been delayed over the years in part due to the logistical difficulties over where to place inmates.

    Dana Kaplan - who Mamdani appointed as the city's "Close Rikers Czar" told the BBC News channel on Friday that his latest proposal is not just about getting rid of a decrepit facility.

    It is also a "generational opportunity" to "build a different type of detention system" and figure out how to detain people more appropriately, she stated.

    The Rikers Island jail complex is perched on a 413 acre (167 hectare) island between Queens and the Bronx, and has earned a variety of nicknames over the years because of its dilapidated conditions, including Gladiator School and Torture Island. The jail has housed a number of high-profile inmates awaiting trial, including Tupac Shakur, DMX and Harvey Weinstein.

    It houses more than 6,500 inmates at a given time. Mamdani hopes to reduce that number to 4,100 - a goal that has been met with skepticism by the New York City correction officers' union.

    Recent findings suggest that "[B]uilding a fresh system that puts an arbitrary cap on the City's available jail beds is ill-conceived, irresponsible and jeopardizes the safety of all New Yorkers, including our Officers," NYC Correction Officers' Benevolent Association said in a statement. "The City cannot keep the jail population at around 4,100 without irresponsibly releasing individuals who committed violent felony charges.".

    "It's actually possible to have fewer people in jail in Newly introduced York City - and that is what we should be planning for," she noted.

    The jail complex has long faced backlash over staffing shortages, crumbling conditions and inmate deaths in the facility, including nine this year. Legislation required the jail to be shuttered by 2027, but Mamdani blamed lags under former Mayor Eric Adams' administration as well as the Covid pandemic for the delays.

    Last year, under Adams, a federal judge removed Rikers from the city's control, appointing an independent outside official to make decisions concerning the facility.

    In an 88-page report released on Friday, Mamdani remarked Rikers was a product of "deteriorating infrastructure" and that officials had a "moral imperative" to close it.

    New York City Council must approve the updated timeline, with members, including the city's speaker, indicating they support the strategy.

    Mamdani's office stated the city would open up four new jails - one in Brooklyn by 2029, two in the Bronx and Queens by 2031 and one in Manhattan by 2032.

    Industry observers note that the mayor's office argues the new, smaller facilities will provide inmates "access to daylight, fresh air and clean space" leading to better outcomes for detainees. The facilities will be easier for families to access as well, as travel to the remote Rikers can take hours.

    Mamdani remarked his administration would work to reduce the number of people being held in jail across Fresh York City, including by offering alternative programmes to detention for some awaiting trial, by making it easier for families to post bail online and by trying to speed up the pretrial legal process.

    He also wants to open up hundreds of beds in therapeutic housing units for prisoners with serious mental health issues.

    Kaplan said Mamdani's administration had already opened 100 therapeutic beds at Bellevue Hospital in Manhattan, moving 100 people off of Rikers Island.

    The proposal involves a large investments: $146m (Â£111m) for mental health and substance use treatment and vocational and education programming inside and outside the jails.

    #58823. Trump admin still won't let Wi-Fi giant TP-Link sell its latest routers in US

    📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 19m • 📚 Deep Dive (3707 w)
    📖 Baca
    Business & Policy ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Ars Technica ↗ Open Full Page

    Trump admin still won't let Wi-Fi giant TP-Link sell its latest routers in US

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 19 min read (3707 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Ars Technica

    ⏱️ ~19 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • TP-Link, which may be the top provider of wireless routers for US homes and small businesses, isn’t allowed to sell its latest Wi-Fi routers in the US.
    • Industry observers note that the rules prevent the import or sale of all upcoming router models that are manufactured, assembled, designed, or developed outside the US.
    • While some of its competitors have obtained exemptions to the ban, TP-Link appears to be having a hard time making its case to government officials.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    TP-Link, which may be the top provider of wireless routers for US homes and small businesses, isn’t allowed to sell its latest Wi-Fi routers in the US. The Trump administration imposed a sweeping ban on foreign-made consumer routers in March 2026, and TP-Link hasn’t been able to obtain an exemption.

    Industry observers note that the rules prevent the import or sale of all upcoming router models that are manufactured, assembled, designed, or developed outside the US. The Trump administration has control over which router makers receive special permission to import and sell new products through a waiver-review process involving the Federal Communications Commission, the Department of Defense, and the Department of Homeland Security.

    While some of its competitors have obtained exemptions to the ban, TP-Link appears to be having a hard time making its case to government officials. Its routers approved before the March 2026 ban remain available for sale in the US, but its newly released Wi-Fi 8 routers cannot be imported or sold.

    Industry observers note that TP-Link’s struggle is not much of a surprise, given its history as a Chinese tech giant and the Trump administration’s focus on reducing reliance on Chinese and other foreign technology. While TP-Link faces political challenges related to the Trump administration’s push for on-shoring, its problems go deeper: It must convince the government its routers aren’t vulnerable to foreign hacking campaigns and that its routers are not Chinese-controlled technology, as suggested at a congressional committee hearing last year.

    TP-Link was founded in 1996 in China but has since split into two companies, with one in the US. The US-based TP-Link established California as its global headquarters in October 2024, months after completing a “formal organizational separation” from the TP-Link entity in China.

    “TP-Link has split from and no longer has any affiliation with TP-LINK Technologies Co., Ltd., which serves the mainland Chinese market. Despite having similar names, these companies have entirely different ownership, management, and operations,” TP-Link indicates.

    TP-Link opened preorders for its first Wi-Fi 8 router, the Archer 8 Ultra, in September, though not in the US. It’s expected to ship this month and costs £899.99 in the UK, or about $1,178. Since it’s priced like a luxury device, its unavailability in the US won’t make a difference to most consumers. But it’s unknown how long it will take TP-Link to gain permission to sell Wi-Fi 8 routers in the US, or whether it will receive permission at all.

    Industry observers note that TP-Link has pledged to assemble all upcoming routers in the US, but convincing Trump officials that it is fully under US control is likely a difficult task. The government reviews of router makers’ requests for waivers, formally called conditional approvals, are shrouded in secrecy. From the outside, it is unclear whether the Trump administration applies consistent security criteria to all companies or whether it grants waivers to favored companies without regard to the actual security of their products.

    In a recent development, companies led by Trump allies Elon Musk and Jeff Bezos fared well in the reviews. SpaceX’s Starlink division obtained a waiver for its routers, while Amazon received a waiver covering routers for its Leo satellite broadband service and the devices sold by its Eero subsidiary. There have been 26 waivers issued so far, covering products made by firms such as Netgear, Asus, Adtran, Calix, Nokia, Micro-Star International, Askey, Zyxel, Humax, and Vantiva.

    Some US lawmakers seem to think the FCC process covers too many products. House Commerce Committee Ranking Member Frank Pallone, Jr. (D-N.J.) and Chairman Brett Guthrie (R-Ky.) proposed legislation in September that would limit the FCC’s authority to place entire categories of equipment on the list of banned products, as it did with routers.

    Recent findings suggest that the Pallone/Guthrie bill would also require the FCC to report to Congress a week before adding any latest technology or service to what’s known as the Covered List and require new additions to include only technologies or services produced or provided by an entity controlled by a foreign adversary. That means China, Russia, North Korea, or Iran.

    “The current process for identifying and barring malicious foreign technology has worked in many cases, but lacks the transparency, consistency, and clarity needed to meet our long-term national security needs as technology rapidly advances,” Pallone and Guthrie remarked in a joint statement.

    The Pentagon declined Ars’ request for comment on TP-Link’s request for an exemption. The FCC and Department of Homeland Security did not provide any comment.

    The US ban on all foreign routers was part of a dramatic expansion of the Covered List, which is managed by the FCC in consultation with the Commerce Department and federal agencies with national security expertise. The Covered List was created by a 2020 law and received its first additions in March 2021. It applies to products that “pose an unacceptable risk to the national security of the United States or the security and safety of United States persons.”.

    In a recent development, for the first few years of the Covered List’s existence, only specific companies were added. This included Chinese device-makers Huawei and ZTE, several video surveillance product makers, the Russian security company Kaspersky Lab, and several Chinese telecom companies. Under the Trump administration, latest additions to the list include entire product categories, regardless of whether a particular vendor has been identified as a risk. In addition to routers, the Covered List right now includes foreign drones, robotic devices, and power inverters.

    A former government official told Ars that the Covered List isn’t as useful as it should be.

    According to recent reports, “The government needs to be able to quickly identify national security risks and, to the extent that they can, you’ve got to give the public and industry guidance on what to do in order to avoid that risk,” noted Betsy McIntyre, a lawyer and consultant who previously worked for the FCC on telecom mergers and at the Department of Justice on national security reviews of foreign investment in telecom. “That’s why I have always loved the Covered List. It’s this great tool. It’s simple. It has so much potential to guide procurement decisions for small businesses, large businesses. It can even help when moms are going to Best Buy and figuring out what kinds of equipment they should be buying.”.

    McIntyre doesn’t like the approach of adding entire categories of products to the list, rather than specific products from individual companies.

    Industry observers note that “The ideal Covered List would be, as soon as there’s a problem, it would be updated,” she said. “They’d name a manufacturer, and then people know: ‘don’t buy this’ or ‘this kind of equipment poses a national security risk.’ It’s a little bit muddled now.”.

    Although the FCC maintains the Covered List, McIntyre said the FCC’s role was set up at the beginning to be “very ministerial.” The FCC would add companies or products to the list based on determinations by national security agencies, with the FCC having no discretion once it received a determination.

    Sources indicate that mcIntyre noted that she was not privy to any of the discussions that led to the broad inclusion of routers this year. It’s not necessarily clear to the public why any particular item is added to the list or why any company receives an exemption, because “the national security decision-making process can be a black box,” she said.

    It has been revealed that TP-Link routers formed the bulk of a botnet controlled by Chinese threat actors, Microsoft noted in 2024. But TP-Link is far from the only router maker whose products have vulnerabilities. Routers made by US companies Cisco and Netgear were part of a botnet of devices hijacked by Chinese state-sponsored attackers in 2023, the Justice Department said after taking action to remove the malware.

    Security expert Bruce Schneier noted there’s no reason to think TP-Link routers are less secure than those of its competitors. “They’re all awful. They’re all equally awful,” he told Ars.

    Computers and smartphones generally have strong security because companies like Apple, Google, and Microsoft “have massive security teams designing these things to be good in the first place and writing patches when flaws are found,” Schneier mentioned.

    With routers, webcams, smart refrigerators, wireless drones, and Internet of Things devices in general, “there’s no one on staff to deal with a security vulnerability… These are just less secure devices because the economics of them doesn’t reward security. The way you patch a lot of your home routers is you throw it away and buy a latest one. That’s the patch mechanism.”.

    When asked about TP-Link facing more scrutiny because of its history as a Chinese tech giant, Schneier noted that router makers are “all Chinese companies… I don’t care what [name] you stick on the box. They’re all made in China.”.

    TP-Link is pledging to assemble routers in the US, though it would still use parts from overseas. Schneier remarked that “these are distinctions that don’t matter that much.”.

    TP-Link states the devices it sells in the US are made in Vietnam. But an April 2025 Bloomberg article noted, “TP-Link confirmed that, aside from components bought in Vietnam that account for 0.5 percent of the total value of inputs to the plant there, all other components are imported from China.”.

    TP-Link declined an interview request from Ars this month. “Aside from what’s already out there, the company doesn’t have any new updates to share right now,” a TP-Link spokesperson told us.

    Sources indicate that TP-Link could sue the government, but litigation can drag out for years. Drone makers have been subject to the same kind of FCC import ban since December 2025, and Chinese drone maker DJI sued the FCC in February. FCC and Justice Department lawyers urged the court to dismiss the lawsuit as “premature,” because the FCC hasn’t made a final decision on a petition that DJI filed with the FCC. The US government’s latest motion to dismiss the lawsuit is still pending with the Ninth Circuit appeals court, and the FCC hasn’t ruled on the petition for reconsideration that DJI filed in January.

    It has been revealed that several developments over the past two years make it unsurprising that TP-Link hasn’t obtained a waiver. US officials reportedly considered a TP-Link ban due to national security risks during the final months of the Biden administration. The government separately probed TP-Link last year in an antitrust investigation reportedly focused on whether it sold goods below cost to gain a dominant share of the US router market.

    The House Select Committee on the Chinese Communist Party held a March 2025 hearing on deterring China’s hacking attacks and improving what the committee called “America’s lackluster cyber defenses.” Rob Joyce, former director of cybersecurity for the National Security Agency, noted in testimony that China is “undercutting our market to deliver Chinese-controlled technologies into our homes” and named TP-Link as the prime example.

    Sources indicate that “TP-Link, the world’s largest manufacturer of commercial Wi-Fi and home routers, has grown to at least 60 percent of the US retail market for Wi-Fi systems and SoHo [Small Office and Home Office] routers compared with about 10 percent of the market at the start of 2019,” he mentioned. “How have they achieved this miraculous growth? They appear to be selling at price points below profitability to drive out the western competition… TP-Link routers were among the various brands exploited by Chinese state-sponsored hackers in the massive Volt, Flax, and Salt Typhoon attacks… We cannot have the software for these prolific devices be written, updated, and controlled by a Chinese company. By law, such a company is subject to the direction of the PRC [People’s Republic of China] Intelligence apparatus. This is a threat we cannot ignore.”.

    TP-Link said in a March 2025 response to Joyce’s comments that its “products are not ‘Chinese-controlled technology,’” that “all of TP-Link’s R&D operations globally are owned and controlled by TP-Link’s US headquarters,” and that “no government—including the PRC—has access to and control over the design and production of TP-Link routers.”.

    It has been revealed that in 2023, the year before Biden administration officials reportedly considered a TP-Link ban, TP-Link boasted of being “the world’s No. 1 Wi-Fi product provider for 12 years running” based on analyst firm IDC’s tracking of worldwide shipments. More recently, TP-Link has argued that estimates of its dominance are wildly inflated, at least in the US.

    TP-Link’s response to Joyce remarked it held “a 36.6 percent unit share and a 31 percent dollar share of the US consumer router market during 2024.” The company claims in a fact sheet that when routers provided to users by Internet service providers are taken into account, “TP-Link’s market share of residential Wi-Fi router sales in North America in 2024 was under 10 percent.”.

    Florida and three other states with Republican attorneys general sued TP-Link last month, alleging that it lied to consumers about connections to China and the risks of its routers being exploited by Chinese state hackers. A group of 21 Republican state AGs also sent a letter to the FCC, urging it to address alleged violations of state laws in its review of TP-Link’s waiver request. TP-Link told the FCC that the “heightened standard” demanded by state attorneys general “would be unattainable to TP-Link or any other router manufacturer in the world.”.

    In a recent development, last month, the FCC warned TP-Link that several of its existing routers exceeded power limits. These include devices already being used by US consumers, such as the Archer BE670 tri-band Wi-Fi 7 router.

    “Based on our evaluation of the purchased samples, we have tentatively determined that TP-Link included false or incorrect information in its applications for these equipment authorizations; and these devices do not operate consistently with the parameters power levels [sic] submitted in the certification applications,” the FCC told TP-Link.

    TP-Link told Bloomberg that any routers exceeding power limits are an aberration and that the four products identified by the FCC account for less than one-third of 1 percent of the company’s total US unit sales this year. Nonetheless, the power-limit investigation related to TP-Link’s existing routers may be a bad sign for its chances of getting a waiver to import and sell Wi-Fi 8 routers.

    TP-Link told reporter Dong Ngo that the FCC tests were “routine spot checks.” But FCC officials may have examined existing TP-Link devices because of the pending request for a waiver from the Covered List.

    “Any time a company has significant requests before the agency, it’s not unusual if the agency is making sure that the company is behaving in a manner the way they expect it to, complying with the rules,” mentioned Jeremy Marcus, a lawyer who spent over 20 years in government in multiple roles, including deputy chief of the FCC Enforcement Bureau.

    Recent findings suggest that marcus declined to discuss TP-Link specifically. He noted that the FCC Office of Engineering and Technology has ongoing market surveillance programs. But when a tech giant has larger concerns pending at the FCC, the Office of Engineering and Technology may “do their own due diligence to make sure that existing equipment is performing the way it’s authorized to,” he said.

    Recent findings suggest that although TP-Link has since gone a bit quiet and declined an interview request from Ars, a company official previously spoke to other publications about the FCC waiver process. TP-Link corporate affairs officer Steve Kovsky told PCMag last month that “there isn’t a lot of clarity” in the government’s demands for US-built technology. Many components used in routers are only available from foreign countries, he noted.

    In a recent development, “There are no published guidelines that say, ‘Well, it could be 25 percent US, or it could be 15 percent US,'” he mentioned. “Or what about, we buy our chipsets for these products from Qualcomm and Broadcom. Is that a US product?”.

    Kovsky’s background is in corporate marketing and communications, and he started at TP-Link a year ago in a contracting role as a senior communications strategist and consultant. He was hired as the corporate affairs officer in June and has been the main public speaker on the firm’s attempts to get a Covered List waiver.

    Industry observers note that kovsky expressed some optimism last month. “We have no problem with the FCC, and are really looking forward to pursuing this, and really setting the standard for transparency, and showing that we have the ability to perform and meet all of these criteria with flying colors,” Kovsky told PCMag. “I don’t know if every manufacturer could say the same thing.”.

    Recent findings suggest that kovsky spoke to The Verge around the same time, defending the firm’s security. “We do not sell customer data or share it with any government ever,” he remarked. “We never will. We do not allow backdoors in our products. We are not susceptible to malware or vulnerabilities to an extent that’s greater than any other manufacturer in this category, to my knowledge.”.

    It has been revealed that kovsky also downplayed TP-Link’s router market share in the US. “It’s about 9 to 10 percent, which is like top three,” he stated. “It’s a good number, but we do not have an overwhelming share of the US market.”.

    Kovsky pleaded with government officials for a quick approval in a letter to the FCC last month. TP-Link is ready to make “a nearly $1 billion investment in America that would result in equipping existing US factories, and ultimately building latest, highly automated manufacturing facilities, to start assembling next-generation Wi-Fi 8 routers in the United States as soon as next year, creating hundreds of new jobs,” he wrote. “TP-Link is proud of this proposal and is poised to unleash this investment upon a grant of its Conditional Approval application.”.

    Because the Trump administration added virtually all routers to the Covered List, each router maker must obtain a determination from the Department of Defense or Department of Homeland Security that its routers do not pose unacceptable national security risks and present a proposal to establish or expand manufacturing in the US.

    Router makers seeking conditional approvals must submit, among other things, details about which countries all of the components and software in its routers come from; details about parts that have only a single source and contingency plans if those suppliers become unavailable; locations of manufacturing and assembly; and a “quantitative assessment of supply chain concentration by country, expressed as both a percentage of total value and production volume.”.

    Router makers must also provide a “justification on why any foreign manufactured router is not at the moment manufactured in the United States, including why these foreign sources were selected and whether alternatives exist,” and a “detailed, time-bound proposal to establish or expand manufacturing in the United States.”.

    Although McIntyre would prefer that the list be focused on individual companies instead of entire product categories, she stated others argue that the process benefits the US because it forces companies to think harder about where they obtain components from and to provide the government with on-shoring aims.

    “I have talked to people who say, ‘Listen, you do these entire class bans, and it’s really forcing companies to really think about their supply chain… You want to have as many of these routers made in the United States as possible, just because you have a little bit more control over what’s going into the router,’” she remarked.

    The FCC said the addition of routers was based on a determination by a White House-convened group of Executive Branch agencies with national security expertise, which said that “malicious state and non-state sponsored cyber attackers have increasingly leveraged the vulnerabilities in small and home office routers produced abroad to carry out direct attacks.” The agencies said that “routers in the United States must have trusted supply chains so we are not providing foreign actors with potential built-in backdoors to American homes, businesses, critical infrastructure, and emergency services.”.

    Although the FCC has generally based Covered List inclusions on determinations by other agencies, McIntyre pointed out an exception. In January 2025, the Commerce Department issued a determination about the risk of connected car hardware and software being controlled by Chinese- or Russian-controlled entities and used its own authority to prohibit transactions involving Chinese or Russian vehicle-connectivity systems.

    After the Commerce determination, the FCC sought comment from the public on whether to add the vehicles to the Covered List. “That is the only example I have found of the FCC doing anything other than just taking what they were given and putting it on the Covered List,” McIntyre said.

    Under the law, the FCC is required to base Covered List decisions on determinations by federal agencies with national security expertise, or the Department of Commerce. With connected cars, the FCC took public comment and has not added the vehicles to the list.

    “We are not required to provide the opportunity for public input on updates to the Covered List under the Commission’s rules, and we have not done so in the past,” the FCC stated in May 2025. “However, because this would be the first addition that does not include the names of specific entities, we believe that offering an opportunity for public input will help promote transparency and good governance.”.

    It has been revealed that the FCC made its first Covered List addition that does not include names of specific entities seven months later, but for drones, not connected cars. The Pallone/Guthrie bill mentioned earlier in this article would limit or prevent future additions that don’t name specific entities.

    “The placement on or removal from the list… of a class or category of information and communications technology or service without reference to an entity that produced or provided that technology shall be deemed a major rule” as defined in the Congressional Review Act (CRA), the bill claims.

    Sources indicate that the CRA lets Congress overturn certain federal actions, including major rules. Pallone and Guthrie’s bill announcement said the Covered List process needs Congressional oversight and that their proposed “changes improve consistency and transparency around the FCC Covered List, ensuring that it targets foreign adversaries and is used as Congress intended to safeguard our national security.”.

    #58820. China, ASEAN countries struggle over South China Sea code of conduct

    📅 22 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1126 w)
