    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Ars Technica ↗ Open Full Page

    Rocket Report: A weekend of ups and downs; Stoke celebrates engine milestone

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 10 min read (1996 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Ars Technica

    ⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Welcome to Edition 9.20 of the Rocket Report!
    • According to recent reports, europe’s leading satellite startup eyes Italian rocket maker.
    • Fulfilling a need … In a statement, ICEYE stated it wants to join forces with Avio to meet Europe’s need for “sovereign space and defense capabilities.” ICEYE manufactures and operates its own satellites for radar surveillance and sells data to commercial customers and national governments, including Ukraine, which uses ICEYE imagery for targeting and tracking Russian troop movements.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Welcome to Edition 9.20 of the Rocket Report! Last weekend was a picture of the US launch business in miniature, and emblematic of the opposing trajectories of two of the nation’s most experienced rocket makers. First, on Saturday, SpaceX completed a perfect midair catch of its Starship upper stage at its launch pad in Texas after spending nearly a day in orbit. The Super Heavy booster was lost at sea, but SpaceX proved it can recover that piece of the rocket on previous flights. While SpaceX showed it is well on the way to fielding a fully reusable rocket, United Launch Alliance suffered its first-ever total launch failure with the Vulcan rocket. That is terrible news for not only ULA, but also the US Space Force and Amazon, which have booked some 70 launches on Vulcan over the next few years. Your faithful correspondents will take a break from the Rocket Report next week for the Thanksgiving holiday, so we’ll see you again the first week of December.

    According to recent reports, europe’s leading satellite startup eyes Italian rocket maker. Finnish satellite developer ICEYE announced Tuesday that it is seeking to buy Italian rocket-maker Avio for more than $2.2 billion in a transaction aimed at creating Europe’s first true vertically integrated end-to-end space firm, Ars reports. Avio builds the Vega C rocket, a solid-fueled launcher designed to carry up to 3.3 metric tons (7,300 pounds) of payload to low-Earth orbit. ICEYE is, by far, the most successful space startup in Europe, with a valuation of more than $12 billion after the company’s most recent fundraising round in June.

    Fulfilling a need … In a statement, ICEYE stated it wants to join forces with Avio to meet Europe’s need for “sovereign space and defense capabilities.” ICEYE manufactures and operates its own satellites for radar surveillance and sells data to commercial customers and national governments, including Ukraine, which uses ICEYE imagery for targeting and tracking Russian troop movements. Most of ICEYE’s satellites have rolled out on SpaceX Falcon 9 rockets. With Falcon 9’s retirement on the horizon, ICEYE’s satellites will need rides to orbit. Avio’s Vega C rocket has a healthy backlog of contracts for European governments, but it hasn’t been a hit commercially. Investment from ICEYE could shore up Avio’s Vega rocket program and perhaps accelerate development of a newly introduced rocket.

    Industry observers note that NATO unveils launch brokerage initiative. The North Atlantic Treaty Organization is contracting commercial rockets and spaceports to grow its satellite launch network and help neutralize risks to the space systems on which it relies, Bloomberg reports. NATO rolled out two initiatives on Tuesday: Starlift, through which participating countries can secure slots on commercial rockets, and the Global Data Marketplace, which will bolster the alliance’s military operations in space with commercial data and services.

    Recent findings suggest that swimming in rolls out … Starlift will allow participating countries—Belgium, Canada, Finland, Germany, Italy, the Netherlands, Norway, Sweden, Turkey, the UK, and South Korea—to pool their military launch requirements and secure launch slots on commercial rockets. The NATO initiative will also prepare and test procedures for short-notice launches, as might be needed in a crisis. Bloomberg reported NATO’s tech agency will offer about $2.7 billion in contracts over the next two years, including to commercial space companies, AI, cyber, and command-and-control networks.

    It has been revealed that stoke wraps up booster engine development. Stoke Space has completed development of its Zenith engine, the methane-fueled powerplant that will propel the company’s medium-class Nova rocket off the launch pad. Stoke made the announcement in a social media post Thursday. “As flight engines clear acceptance testing, we’re shipping them down to Cape Canaveral for integration with Nova’s first stage—every week,” Stoke said. Seven Zenith engines will power the Nova rocket’s reusable first stage booster, combining to generate about 700,000 pounds of thrust at full throttle.

    Industry observers note that all eyes on Stage 2 … Stoke announced it cleared a “proto-qualification” milestone on Stage 1 earlier this year. Stage 2 is undergoing cryogenic proof testing and a hot-fire test campaign at Stoke’s test complex in rural Washington. Nova’s second stage is the real innovation, with a unique arrangement of 24 thrusters surrounding a regeneratively cooled heat shield to protect it during reentry back into Earth’s atmosphere. With this, Stoke aims to fully reuse both Nova stages. The first launch is currently expected sometime next year.

    Soyuz flies from Russia’s Far East. A Soyuz-2.1b rocket made its first and only launch from Russia’s Vostochny Cosmodrome this year, RussianSpaceWeb.com reports. The rocket’s Fregat upper stage deployed a new pair of high-resolution imaging satellites, along with a cluster of smaller payloads, following liftoff from Russia’s Vostochny launch base on November 14 (local time). Vostochny, located in Russia’s Far East, hosted its first space launch in 2016. By some measures, Russia spent more than $5 billion building Vostochny, only to use it for an average of two debuts per year.

    Recent findings suggest that what was onboard? … Soyuz and Fregat carried two dual-use imaging surveillance satellites. A pair of CubeSat-class satellites for a Russian arms manufacturer were also onboard. These satellites are owned by NPO Kaisant, which specializes in drone communications and counter-drone weapons. NPO Kaisant notes the satellites will join a constellation providing secure communications to Russian drones over Ukraine. A total of 12 secondary payloads were reported to be onboard, according to Roscosmos.

    According to recent reports, china’s LandSpace reports rocket reuse milestone. Three months after landing its first orbital-class rocket booster, Chinese rocket company LandSpace claims it has completed “ground acceptance and testing” of the nine methane-fueled engines recovered from the first stage of its Zhuque-3 rocket, according to Guandian News, a Chinese outlet focusing on the country’s financial and economic sector. The engines were disassembled, inspected, refurbished, reassembled, and retested after flying to space and back in August.

    But wait … LandSpace’s Zhuque-3 is one of two Chinese rockets to successfully land its booster after an orbital launch attempt. The company did not say whether any of the nine engines will fly again, but don’t count on the entire Zhuque-3 booster stage from the August flight making another trip to space. The Zhuque-3 first stage toppled over soon after a seemingly flawless touchdown at LandSpace’s downrange recovery zone in northwestern China. Based on this week’s news, it appears engineers were able to salvage the engines.

    According to recent reports, spaceX makes a historic catch. SpaceX, nearly a quarter of a century after its founding, took a hugely significant step toward developing and optimizing a massive, rapidly reusable rocket with the first successful catch of its enormous Starship upper stage on November 14, Ars reports. It’s hard to overstate the significance of the moment. SpaceX’s ability to recover and quickly relaunch Starships and Super Heavy boosters is central to all of the tech giant’s lofty commercial ambitions and many of America’s high-level strategic imperatives, from national security to maintaining dominance in space exploration.

    What was it like to be there? … Ars Space Editor Eric Berger covered the launch and catch of Starship from a nearby perch at Starbase, Texas. “Watching Starship launch from here a little less than a day earlier, and knowing it had orbited the planet multiple times, added to the sense of unreality in seeing this spaceship return to Earth under its own power and be captured by the tower,” Berger writes. “It felt like stepping into the future. SpaceX has dazzled us before by landing rockets on barges and returning humans to space with Crew Dragon. But this flight took things to another level. Starships are huge. They carry a huge amount of energy coming back from orbit. And until a few years ago, it seemed beyond fantastical to think about capturing a rocket with what are essentially outsized chopsticks. Nevertheless, it happened.”.

    Vulcan fails to deliver for Amazon. United Launch Alliance’s Vulcan rocket and 40 Amazon Leo broadband satellites fell back to Earth minutes after liftoff Sunday, a crushing setback that will ripple across all sectors of the US space industry, Ars reports. Aside from ULA itself, the fallout from the failure will strike the US military and Amazon hardest. Sunday’s mission was the first of 38 Vulcan releases booked by Amazon to build out its network of broadband Internet satellites aimed at competing with SpaceX’s Starlink. Vulcan is also on contract to launch roughly half of the US Space Force’s national security missions over the next few years.

    According to recent reports, identifying the cause … ULA said Wednesday that the failure was caused by inadequate fuel supply to the first stage engines, Ars reports in a follow-up story. “ULA has completed an initial integrated review of flight data from the Leo 1 launch anomaly that occurred last Sunday,” the organization said in a statement. “While work remains to determine cause, preliminary indications are that the low booster thrust was the result of inadequate fuel supply from the vehicle to the BE-4 engines, not from the performance of the engines.” This is fantastic news for Blue Origin, which builds the BE-4 and uses a similar design on its own New Glenn rocket. Vulcan’s solid rocket boosters also performed as expected Sunday after experiencing nozzle failures on two prior Vulcan flights.

    Recent findings suggest that google taps Blue Origin for AI launch. Blue Origin announced Thursday that its Upcoming Glenn rocket will launch data center satellites for Google in 2029 as part of that company’s Project Suncatcher program, Ars reports. Google disclosed it was working on scalable orbiting data centers about a year ago and characterized the project as one of its research “moonshots.” The mission on New Glenn is designed to deploy satellites, each with computing capacity at roughly the scale of a data center rack, into Sun-synchronous orbit where they can receive nearly continuous solar energy.

    According to recent reports, hitching a ride … Google snatched up a ride on New Glenn just as US commercial heavy-lift rockets are filling up their capacity through the year 2030. The Google mission will fly on the 7×2 variant of the New Glenn rocket, the smaller version of the vehicle that has rolled out three times to date. The purpose of the 2029 launch will likely be to test the ability to network solar-powered satellites equipped with AI chips and demonstrate machine-learning compute in space. Perhaps the bigger question for Google is not whether it can make this technology work—but whether it is tenable for a manufacturer to have ambitions for a large constellation of orbital data centers in the 2030s without its own launch vehicle.

    Sources indicate that relativity makes progress with Terran R. Another fresh rocket is moving closer to the launch pad. Relativity Space’s partially reusable Terran R rocket could launch sometime next year if engineers can finish development with no major setbacks. Relativity posted an revision on YouTube this week, detailing several recent achievements at several of the tech giant’s locations across the country. At Relativity headquarters in Southern California, teams have completed Terran R’s first stage thrust structure with a full set of 13 Aeon engines, fluid lines, and avionics. The engine compartment is now being integrated with Stage 1 tankage. Terran R’s second stage recently completed its first all-up test firing at Stennis Space Center, Mississippi.

    Meanwhile, at Cape Canaveral … Relativity is also moving forward with the Terran R launch pad at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station, Florida. The launch pad’s lightning protection towers are now complete, as is the steel framing for Terran R’s launch table. Work continues on the rocket’s transporter-erector, strongback, and the launch pad’s propellant storage tanks.

    November 20: Long March 8A | SatNet LEO Group | Wenchang Space Launch Site, China | 11:59 UTC.

    November 21: Falcon 9 | USSF-317 | Vandenberg Space Force Base, California | 02:32 UTC.

    November 21: Long March 6C | Unknown Payload | Taiyuan Satellite Launch Center, China | 03:50 UTC.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The Nasdaq lost trillions in value, with the AI startup’s IPO failing to buoy it as investors question huge sums being poured into AI buildout.
    • Who are Anthropic’s seven co-founders, now worth $180bn?
    • As Anthropic’s stock dropped during its second day of trading, the wider stock market dipped with it.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The Nasdaq lost trillions in value, with the AI startup’s IPO failing to buoy it as investors question huge sums being poured into AI buildout.

    Who are Anthropic’s seven co-founders, now worth $180bn?

    As Anthropic’s stock dropped during its second day of trading, the wider stock market dipped with it. On Friday, the Nasdaq Composite erased all its gains for 2026 and closed down 5% from its value on 1 January. The Dow Jones Industrial Average and S&P 500 closed in correction territory.

    Anthropic’s record-breaking IPO failed to stem a global sell-off in AI-linked companies, and the tech-heavy Nasdaq erased some $4tn in market value this week, according to the Wall Street Journal.

    Recent findings suggest that shares in the frontier AI tech giant behind the Claude chatbot, which floated in the US on Thursday, fell by 9% on Friday, ceding most of the gains from the biggest initial public offering in history. They dropped to $88.30, towards the $83 level at which Anthropic priced its stock market debut.

    It has been revealed that anthropic’s first two days as a listed organization have been volatile. Its shares jumped by 17% on Thursday, after briefly surging by almost 40% when trading in the firm began.

    According to recent reports, US technology stocks followed Anthropic down on Friday, with the memory chipmaker SanDisk falling 14% and rival Micron down 12%. Nvidia fell 14%, eliminating hundreds of billions of dollars in market cap.

    Recent findings suggest that neil Wilson, a UK investor strategist at Saxo, said there was “just relentless selling in tech”. He warned: “Anthropic shares tumbled to take an $85 handle as the post-IPO euphoria gives way to the reality of a steep sell-off across the tech and AI space that shows no sign of easing just yet.”.

    Industry observers note that global markets slumped on Friday too; Asian stock markets recorded their worst week since 2020, as shares in big chip companies fell. In Taiwan, stocks dropped 6.7% to hit their lowest point since mid-April, with the chip maker TSMC down about 6%.

    The scale of the decline in Taiwan prompted the chair of its stock exchange to pledge to ensure the stable operation ⁠of capital markets, and reassure investors they should remain confident in the fundamentals of Taiwanese companies.

    In Japan, the Nikkei index fell 5%, while South Korea’s tech-heavy Kospi index lost 5.5%. Shares in the tech investor SoftBank had their worst day in more than two years, down 14.5% in Tokyo, amid worries around its aggressive bets on AI.

    Sources indicate that european stock markets posted their biggest weekly loss since March 2025, with the pan-European Stoxx 600 dropping 1.9% on Friday. London’s blue-chip stock index hit a five-month low.

    The sell-off followed losses on Wall Street on Thursday, where the main indices all fell by more than 2% on a day dominated by Anthropic’s IPO.

    Chris Beauchamp, the chief market analyst at the investing and trading platform IG, mentioned Anthropic could be “draining market liquidity”, as investors sell shares in other companies to raise funds to pay for stock in the newly floated AI firm.

    “The slide from yesterday’s highs sends a message that there might be more at work here than investors realise, and while brokers are scrambling to buy more, that liquidity has to come from somewhere, and the other tech names may be the first ones to feel the pressure,” Beauchamp said.

    Anthropic’s flotation has failed to ease worries around the AI trade, as investors increasingly question whether companies can deliver the returns necessary to justify the billions of dollars being poured into the AI buildout.

    Daniela Hathorn, a senior market analyst at Capital.com, stated: “The IPO demonstrated that demand for AI exposure remains strong, but it has not been enough to overcome concerns about elevated valuations, profitability and the sustainability of investment spending.

    Sources indicate that “The broader market mood has shifted from buying the dip towards questioning whether the correction has further to run. The weakness in equal-weighted indices suggests that selling pressure is no longer confined to a handful of technology giants, while Europe’s recent outperformance has also faded.”.

    Nvidia shares fell byafter California served the chip company with a subpoena as part of an investigation into whether its advanced semiconductors ended up in China.

    Britain’s FTSE 100 share index dropped by 5.1% this week, its biggest weekly fall since the start of the Iran war.

    Fears that US central bankers may raise interest rates to fight inflation have lifted the dollar to a 19-month high, and pushed down the gold price – with gold on track for its worst week since March.

    Bitcoin hit its lowest level in four months, dropping below the $60,000 point for the first time since early July.

    Tech Report: Don't throw away your old Xbox — Do this instead

    📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1546 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Engadget

    ⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In a recent development, letting old pieces of tech go is never easy, especially when you have fond memories of the original Xbox.
    • Recent findings suggest that make your Xbox One your go-to streaming box for the bedroom!
    • According to recent reports, if we're talking Xbox One, you can download and enjoy many streaming services on Microsoft's last-gen console, including Netflix, Disney+, Amazon Prime Video, Hulu and Paramount+.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a recent development, letting old pieces of tech go is never easy, especially when you have fond memories of the original Xbox. But no matter how much you loved shooting seven shades of alien goo out of the Covenant in Halo: Combat Evolved, it's unlikely you're still using a 25-year-old console on a daily basis. If you no longer touch your OG Xbox, Xbox 360 or Xbox One, as long as it's working, there are far better options than just tossing it out.

    Recent findings suggest that make your Xbox One your go-to streaming box for the bedroom! Go retro — dust off that Xbox 360 and play those obscure DVD collections you've been hoarding for years! Many Xbox controllers can even be used to enjoy the best PC games! You could obviously make cash for your old console on auctioning sites like eBay. Or here's a thought: How about gifting your past-gen Xbox to a thrift store/charity shop? Your old Xbox deserves more respect than being dumped in a dustbin.

    According to recent reports, if we're talking Xbox One, you can download and enjoy many streaming services on Microsoft's last-gen console, including Netflix, Disney+, Amazon Prime Video, Hulu and Paramount+. Skip back to Xbox 360 and sadly, you're mostly out of luck.

    Provided you don't have a relative who is right now begging for your old console, why not keep it? These past-gen machines are still perfectly good bedroom streaming boxes, with the added bonus that you can still still play classics on them — like Aussie-set open-world racer Forza Horizon 3 — from the comfort of your sheets.

    Industry observers note that xbox consoles have never been associated with watching physical media as much as their PlayStation counterparts. The PS2 was the DVD machine — the first console to embrace a media format that would comprehensively replace video tapes. Did the original Xbox also support DVDs? In a fiddly way... yes. You needed Microsoft's official Xbox DVD Movie Playback Kit, which came with an awkward dongle that needed to be plugged into a controller port to get it working. Not exactly an elegant solution.

    If you're reading this, it's highly unlikely you're trying to repurpose the 25-year-old OG Xbox as a DVD player in an age of 4K Blu-ray players, but if you have kept either an Xbox 360 or Xbox One, those make a whole lot more sense as back-up media players. The 360 will happily play DVDs straight out of the box with zero tinkering required.

    As for the Xbox One, it also plays DVDs and Blu-rays/4K Blu-rays, although the latter media type requires a free Blu-ray app download from the Microsoft Store. I used to occasionally watch UHD discs on my old Xbox One X, and the supercharged console provided perfectly decent UHD movie experiences with my 4K Blu-rays.

    Recent findings suggest that microsoft has done a tremendous job with backwards-compatibility for several generations. Skip back to Xbox One X, and the firm offered free 4K upgrades for select original Xbox games and 360 titles. These gratis updates include some absolute bangers, like Crackdown, Conker: Live & Reloaded, Halo: Reach, Red Dead Redemption, Mirror's Edge, and many more (well, provided you still own the game).

    In total, 13 OG Xbox games got Xbox One X Enhanced features, while 21 Xbox 360 titles received similar big time resolution boosts thanks to the supercharged console's 6 TFLOPS. For context, the Xbox Series X can tap into 12.15 TFLOPS of GPU power.

    Industry observers note that the Xbox One X, Xbox One and Xbox One S will all play an impressive 632 Xbox 360 games! Microsoft's backward compatibility program deserves all the flowers. Though sadly, Xbox has mostly dropped its commitment to adding new original Xbox and 360 titles to Game Pass since late 2021.

    According to recent reports, the Xbox 360 remains an excellent console for retro fans. Though you'll need a hard drive so that the console can store emulation profiles, around 480 original Xbox games can be enjoyed on the 360. That's pretty impressive considering Microsoft's colossal black box released just shy of 1,000 titles over the course of its life. Sony's commitment to backwards-combability has rarely impressed on the other hand, but you still shouldn't throw away an old PlayStation either.

    Recent findings suggest that let's be honest. There's no way you're actually taking the title of this article literally. If you are legitimately thinking about disposing of your old Xbox like it was yesterday's milk, please recycle it in a safe and eco-safe manner instead. Before you needlessly boot away your console, consider gifting it to someone else. Think of all those who could benefit from an aging Xbox. Young relatives! Charities! Children's hospitals! Your Xbox donation could genuinely make a kid's Christmas.

    Industry observers note that of course, if you could use the extra money, the Xbox One X still goes for upwards of $150 on eBay. Reputable buy-back sites like Back Market Trade-in will give you cash for your console. The site at the moment accepts pretty much every Xbox in existence (though broken units obviously won't fetch you much). If your Xbox One X is in flawless condition and comes with a controller and 1GB of storage, you can currently net a pretty tasty $185.

    It has been revealed that sadly, Back Market isn't the place to sell an old Xbox 360. At time of writing, even if it's in great condition and comes with a controller, the site will only pony up a pathetic $3 for the classic console. Your best chance of raking in some folding money for that old 360 is by selling it on auction sites like eBay and Swappa.

    Unless we're talking about the OG Xbox "Duke" controller, gamepads since the Xbox 360 generation can generally be repurposed to work on gaming PCs. The wired Xbox 360 controller should work just fine with a Windows 11 PC as long as you plug it into one of your rig's USB ports  — Steam is still very good at recognizing old school gamepad layouts, especially in Major Picture Mode. With non-wireless 360 controllers, you'll likely need a cheap Microsoft wireless receiver.

    There is a chance the Massive Boy OG 2001 Xbox controller can function with a Series machine, yet it demands precision work. Getting the 2001 Duke to play nice with an Xbox Series X or S requires a special adapter and third-party software. Compared to this hassle, a Xbox 360 pad should still get along with most modern, Steam-compliant PCs without much issue. Well, as long as you've taken care of said peripheral over the years.

    Xbox One controllers obviously work on Xbox Series X/S consoles, so it's unlikely you're going to throw them aside just because they lack a dedicated Share button. You can pair a Xbox One gamepad to a PC either through a USB cable, Bluetooth connection or picking up the Xbox Wireless Adapter for a hand-free wireless experience that's more reliable than BT.

    Recent findings suggest that if you've finally decided to sell your old Xbox, then you might want to back up your old saves. More importantly, to protect your privacy/delete credit cards you might have stored on the console, you must factory reset your system before selling it.

    Provided your Xbox One is connected to the interwebs, backing up saves is an idiot-proof process before the major step of a factory reset. Your console automatically backs up game saves every time you sign into your console. To secure old saves for the last time before selling your Xbox One, make sure it's online and sign into your usual account. Then it's a case of briefly opening any game you want to keep data from, let your console's "Syncing data" message finish, save and quit out of the game, and you're good to go. If you then decide to buy an Xbox Series X or S, you can download this data from the cloud.

    In a recent development, now it's time to factory reset your Xbox One. Navigate to Profile & system > Settings > System > Console info > Reset console. Choose Reset and remove everything (which deletes all apps, games and local saves). Your Xbox One will be wiped clean.

    Sources indicate that if you're keen on keeping old Xbox 360 saves, plug an empty USB drive into the console, then go to Settings > System > Storage > and choose Configure Now. The 360 will format the drive in its proprietary FAT32 system, at which you can go back to Storage > Hard Drive > Games and Apps. From here, simply select the games whose data you want to preserve, then click Copy > USB Storage Device.

    To factory reset your Xbox 360, head to Settings > System > Storage, select your hard drive, press Y for Device Options, then select Format. If the console asks you for the serial number at this point, you can find it from System > Console Settings > System Info and note it down. Once your 360 has been formatted, it's ready to sell.

    With all of these steps complete, your old Xbox is now good to move on to its next owner.

    The three officers were seen on video beating up music producer Michel Zecler in his studio.

    Three French police officers have been convicted of beating up a black music producer six years ago in Paris in what the court upheld as an aggravated circumstance of racism.

    The three were also found guilty of signing a falsified police report stating that the producer - Michel Zecler, 47 - had violently resisted their attempt to arrest him.

    Their lies were exposed because the whole scene at Zecler's recording studio was caught on CCTV, revealing the producer had suffered some 30 punches, kicks and baton strikes while offering little resistance at all.

    Aurelien Lapersonne, 29, Philippe Tondeux, 50, and Pierre Plantier, 37, all received five year sentences, with different amounts suspended.

    Sources indicate that lapersonne had three years of his sentence suspended and Tondeux three and a half years suspended. Plantier had four years suspended, and will serve his one year with an ankle monitor.

    All were told they could never serve in the police again.

    The case became a cause cÃ©lÃ¨bre for critics of the police, who say it exposed systematic racism among officers. With police again facing criticism for alleged use of excessive force in stopping recent protests, the verdict was hotly awaited by Zecler's supporters.

    Much depended in the two-week trial on Zecler's own testimony that the officers called him a racial slur during the beating.

    In a recent development, this was denied by the three policemen, who in court admitted the beating and the faked report but denied there was a racial motivation. But the court preferred the evidence of the producer, because - unlike the police - everything else he mentioned was verifiably true.

    Because the racist element was accepted by the court, the sentences were toughened.

    The case was heard by a panel of five judges.

    Recent findings suggest that the incident took place during the Covid lockdown in 2020. Zecler was accused by the officers for not wearing a mask when doing so was obligatory as he approached his studio on foot.

    They later claimed his behaviour aroused their suspicions, and they thought he might be carrying drugs. No evidence of this emerged.

    According to recent reports, after Zecler entered the lobby, the police followed - without a warrant - and tried to bring him outside. Zecler refused to go out, and the beating ensued. Zecler cried for help and some people appeared from the basement and pushed the police outside.

    It has been revealed that the officers then smashed a glass pane and sent a tear-gas grenade into the building, forcing those inside to come out - after which Zecler was again hit. He was then arrested.

    During the trial Zecler remarked had it not been for the CCTV video, he would have been in court not as a victim but as a potential criminal.

    Industry observers note that in their last words before the court, all three police officers apologised for what they had done. Tondeux said he was sorry "for the image of the police that I have given".

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Lenders backing SpaceX’s latest $43 billion debt package, which is secured by its advanced AI chips, have tried to bar Elon Musk from firing the collateral into space as part of his blueprint for orbital data centers.
    • Recent findings suggest that the world’s richest man has outlined ambitious plans to power AI models with data centers cooled by the vacuum of space.
    • Industry observers note that spaceX has mentioned it aims to use the chips involved in the debt deal on Earth.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Lenders backing SpaceX’s latest $43 billion debt package, which is secured by its advanced AI chips, have tried to bar Elon Musk from firing the collateral into space as part of his blueprint for orbital data centers.

    Recent findings suggest that the world’s richest man has outlined ambitious plans to power AI models with data centers cooled by the vacuum of space. That will require packing satellites full of advanced chips.

    Industry observers note that spaceX has mentioned it aims to use the chips involved in the debt deal on Earth. But lenders have expressed concerns that if the group later decided to shoot the valuable chips that underpin their loans into space, it would prevent them from reclaiming and selling the semiconductors in the event of a default, according to people familiar with the matter.

    It is uncertain whether the provision was included in the finalized documents.

    The bonds were issued by a special purpose vehicle designed to keep the debt off SpaceX’s balance sheet and preserve its investment-grade credit rating.

    The proposed debt covenant presented potential legal challenges for SpaceX’s ambitions to build data centers in space, highlighting the uncharted territory that investors need to navigate when financing the nascent asset class.

    SpaceX sold more than $30 billion of the debt to large investors on Thursday as part of a financing package dubbed “Project Saturn.” The largest portion of the debt package was a $25 billion investment-grade bond backed by SpaceX’s five-year lease payment for the Nvidia chips.

    In a recent development, the debt was sold at 3.45 percentage points above US Treasuries, indicating a total yield of about 8.3 percent, the people noted. SpaceX’s corporate debt maturing in 2031, meanwhile, traded at a yield of about 7.2 percent on Thursday.

    The newest bonds will mature in 2032, but the principal will be paid off in less than four years—an arrangement that was designed to reduce credit risks for lenders, the people added.

    More than $19 billion of the bonds already secured commitments prior to Thursday, including $4 billion from Pimco.

    In a recent development, apollo and Goldman Sachs, which led the transaction, declined to comment. Pimco declined to comment. SpaceX did not respond to a request for comment.

    Funds managed and advised by BlackRock, Goldman Sachs Asset Management, and KKR have also made anchor commitments in the transaction, according to SpaceX.

    SpaceX prepares to use the chips in US data centers majority-owned, controlled, and operated by SpaceX, according to a rating report issued by Moody’s.

    Moody’s assigned the debt an A3 rating, one notch above SpaceX’s own credit rating. KBRA rated the debt A-minus.

    The credit rating agencies attributed the A-tier rating in part to “hell-or-high-water” clauses that prevent SpaceX from walking away from the lease.

    “The SpaceX GPU deal appears cleverly structured and should appeal to a panoply of buyers, potentially including deep pools of insurance capital seeking attractive yield on investment-grade debt,” mentioned Grant Nachman, chief investment officer at Shorecliff Asset Management.

    “This transaction could prove a harbinger of future issuances,” he noted.

    Additional reporting by Jill R Shah in Latest York.

    • Your Ring doorbell can be so much more than just a doorbell.
    • The Ring's compatibility with so many smart home devices can make your life much more convenient by simply pairing them and controlling them all through the Ring app.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Your Ring doorbell can work in tandem with lots of other smart devices.

    Your Ring doorbell can be so much more than just a doorbell. Of course you're familiar with its helpful functions, like high-resolution video up to 4K, Live View, Two-way Talk, 3D Motion Detection and night vision. What you may not know is that your Ring doorbell can seamlessly connect to all kinds of other smart home gadgets.

    The Ring's compatibility with so many smart home devices can make your life much more convenient by simply pairing them and controlling them all through the Ring app.

    Recent findings suggest that why limit your view to just your porch when you can pair wired and wireless cameras throughout your entire property? Ring alone offers more than two dozen security camera options to pair with your doorbell, including indoor and outdoor spotlight and floodlight cameras. If you're looking to pair a camera not made by Ring, you can do so through the Ring Alarm Pro Base Station and Ring ONVIF support. This enables your Ring system to pair with dozens of other brands, as long as their cameras are ONVIF-compatible.

    Industry observers note that besides cameras, your Ring doorbell is directly compatible with Ring panic buttons, window and door sensors, glass break sensors, sump pump monitors, smoke and carbon monoxide listeners, and air-quality monitors — all controllable through the Ring app — for even more peace of mind. It's notable to note, however, that some of these sensors and accessories may require the Ring Alarm Base Station hub to connect directly with the Ring app. It's a good idea to check your Ring app to find out which accessories are directly compatible.

    Industry observers note that you can also connect certain smart locks directly through the Ring app without needing the Ring Alarm Base Station. If you already have the Ring Alarm Base Station, however, your options increase quite a bit as more manufacturers make smart locks that can be connected to your Ring through the base station via Z-Wave radio frequencies. These locks allow you to lock and unlock your door through the Ring app, a PIN or your key.

    Sources indicate that through the Ring app, you can set up a wide range of lighting options, like outdoor spotlights, steplights, floodlights, wall lights and path lights... even some that are solar-powered. By adding outdoor lighting options, you not only improve your Ring doorbell's camera performance with extra light, but you can also create customized lighting zones, turn lights on and off when you're not home, and program the lights to illuminate when motion is detected.

    Industry observers note that if your home is already equipped with landscape lighting, you can still connect it to your Ring system through the Ring transformer so you can control it through the Ring app. Third-party wireless smart bulbs and other lighting accessories, however, can't be directly connected through the Ring app. But there are workarounds. For example, with the Ring outdoor smart plug, you can turn any "dumb" lights (like most holiday lighting and inflatables) into smart ones by simply plugging them into the smart plug and controlling them with the Ring app.

    Taking advantage of your Ring doorbell isn't limited to outdoor devices. For example, if you own a compatible smart thermostat, you can connect it to your Ring app and control your home's climate right from the Ring dashboard in your app.

    And if you want a better look at what's going on outside your home, there's no better way than on a big-screen smart TV. Through an Amazon Fire TV or Fire TV Stick and the Alexa app, all it takes is a simple voice command through your Alexa remote to show you the front door. Fire TV systems even support picture-in-picture, which pops onto your screen as soon as your doorbell button is pushed. But Ring viewing is also available with newer Samsung Smart TVs through Samsung's SmartThings smart home platform. While the experience isn't quite as smooth as with Fire TVs, the SmartThings app does let you connect your Ring doorbell and manually open the camera to view it on the SmartThings dashboard on your TV.

    Industry observers note that A very useful — and underappreciated — device you can pair with your Ring doorbell is a smart water valve, which allows you to remotely shut off your water supply in the event of a leak to prevent potentially disastrous flooding. Installation requires plumbing the smart water valve into the main water line and then setting up the valve through the Moen Smart Water app. Ring also integrates with some third-party Z-Wave smart water valves.

    It has been revealed that yes, you can even bring Ring technology into your vehicle with the Ring Car Cam and the Ring Car Tracker and Alarm. The dual-facing Car Cam mounts onto your dashboard and keeps an eye on your surroundings, whether the car is parked or in motion. The Car Tracker and Alarm plugs right into your vehicle's OBD-II port and sends push notifications if there are disturbances, including physical impact, a door that's been forced open or towing. This device also offers GPS tracking of your car on your Ring dashboard. Both car accessories are easily integrated into the Ring app so you can keep tabs on everything right on your phone.

    Sources indicate that you may already have a smart garage door opener for your home, but pairing it with your Ring doorbell makes life just a little bit easier. Compatible several major garage door opener brands, the Ring app essentially serves as a shortcut for your garage door, so you have quick access to check on your home.

    By integrating the apps, you can instantly check the status of your garage door on the Ring app dashboard as you view your doorbell and/or camera feeds. This also lets you control your garage door right from your Ring screen, so you can open and close it without using your garage door app. A nice bonus is that this app integration also delivers access to Amazon Key in-garage delivery, which provides Amazon drivers with access to your garage door and allows them to slip your packages securely into your garage before closing the door.

    Industry observers note that you've probably noticed that Ring doorbells are easily paired with Amazon services and devices. That's because Amazon owns Ring, so that effortless integration is intentional by design. And it's quite convenient if you own an Echo Show, Echo Dot or Fire TV. By syncing your Ring doorbell with your Alexa-controlled Amazon device, you can easily set up announcements whenever someone is at your front door, instantly view the live stream of your camera by simply asking Alexa to show you the front door and even communicate with whoever is at your front door through any Alexa speaker... all without ever having to look at your phone.

    The Alexa integration is also beneficial if you want to connect third-party devices and gadgets that aren't directly compatible with your Ring doorbell. These include smart lights and bulbs, smart plugs and switches, thermostats, locks, and TVs. All you need is the Alexa app to set it all up and view it in your Ring app.

    Super-hot rock geothermal could end data center energy woes

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1021 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: TechCrunch

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Geothermal startups are in a race to see who can tap the deepest, hottest rocks.
    • The broader markets got their first taste of enhanced geothermal earlier this year when Fervo Energy went public.
    • Recent findings suggest that geothermal has become a darling among investors, tech companies, and even the Trump administration.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Geothermal startups are in a race to see who can tap the deepest, hottest rocks. The winners could power the next phase of the grid, data centers and all.

    The broader markets got their first taste of enhanced geothermal earlier this year when Fervo Energy went public. But this week was all about super-hot rock geothermal.

    Recent findings suggest that geothermal has become a darling among investors, tech companies, and even the Trump administration. The basic technology has been around for decades, but advances in drilling techniques borrowed from the oil and gas industry has supercharged it. The U.S. has plenty of potential, too, with up to 57 terawatts of generating capacity, more than enough to power the next wave of AI data centers.

    An emerging class of geothermal energy, known as super-hot rock, could help the industry unlock much of that potential.

    The secret to super-hot rock geothermal is what happens to water at extreme depths. As it gets closer to the superheated core of the Earth, both temperature and pressure rise significantly. When they get high enough, ordinary water turns into a supercritical fluid — a sort of gaseous-liquid state that can carry tremendous amounts of energy. A single super-hot rock well could generate 15 megawatts of electricity or more.

    Industry observers note that super-hot rock geothermal is inching closer to commercial reality. Quaise Energy mentioned on Tuesday that it had landed Google as a customer. The hyperscaler said it would pay more than $500 million to secure 50 megawatts of power from a Quaise project in central Oregon, which will tap into searing heat three miles deep.

    Google is paying a premium for the amount of power Quaise will deliver, but that’s in line with the tech giant’s strategy of getting in early with potential suppliers. For instance, it was an investor in and an early customer of Fervo.

    Sources indicate that meanwhile, on Monday, Khosla-backed Mazama Energy declared it had figured out how to keep its drill heads cool as they tap into super-hot rocks. And last week, XGS Energy was given a grant by the Department of Energy to develop and refine materials, well designs, and models to improve reliability at depths where super-hot rock exists.

    XGS is dipping its toes in the super-hot waters, while Mazama and Quaise have made it their core focus, though they’re taking very different approaches.

    Industry observers note that quaise’s technology sounds like science fiction: Starting at about 2.5 miles deep, the company will swap out its conventional drill bit for one powered by a gyrotron, bombarding rock with millimeter-wave radiation and turning it into ash. The hope is that the technology can make drilling under super-hot conditions cost-effective, something that’s challenging with traditional metal drill bits, which wear out faster at those temperatures.

    Mazama, on the other hand, thinks that traditional drill bits will work just fine if they can be kept cool.

    Industry observers note that the startup’s newly revealed technology, Carbon Chill, uses carbon dioxide in place of water-based drilling “mud” to keep the bit cool. At those depths and temperatures, the carbon dioxide turns supercritical, allowing it to hold significant amounts of energy. Just above the drill bit, the CO2 flows through a valve that looks similar to a rocket nozzle. As the gas flows through the valve and expands on the other end, the expansion rapidly cools it, allowing it to absorb significant amounts of heat. The CO2 also removes drill cuttings on its trip to the surface, where it’s filtered and reused.

    In both cases, Quaise and Mazama are betting that their technology could leapfrog today’s state-of-the-art commercial geothermal power plants. By going deeper and hotter, they’re hoping to get substantially more power out of each well. Given that drilling accounts for about a quarter to a third of a geothermal power plant’s total costs, drilling fewer wells could make a project more competitive.

    It has been revealed that investors have been betting that the technologies will soon prove themselves. Quaise has raised more than $270 million from investors, including Prelude Ventures, Collaborative Fund, and Engine Ventures, with Vinod Khosla stepping in as an angel investor, according to PitchBook. Mazama has raised $171 million from investors, including Khosla Ventures, Doerr Capital, and Bill Gates.

    As with any new technology, there’s some risk that the new techniques won’t pay off. But early results suggest they will — Mazama drilled its second well 80% faster than its first, and its CO2-cooling tech cut drilling time another 20%, co-founder and CEO Sriram Vasantharajan told TechCrunch.

    That, plus Google’s vote of confidence in Quaise, suggests the race to super-hot rock geothermal is, well, heating up.

    COP31: Climate deal 'not adopted,' summit president states

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 12 min read (2459 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

    ⏱️ ~12 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Delegates from nearly 200 countries failed to reach an agreement despite prolonging the talks.
    • The summit's president acknowledges that a deal was 'not adopted'.
    • The final draft presented at the summit in Antalya, Turkey omitted any mention of fossil fuels.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Delegates from nearly 200 countries failed to reach an agreement despite prolonging the talks.

    The summit's president acknowledges that a deal was 'not adopted'.

    The final draft presented at the summit in Antalya, Turkey omitted any mention of fossil fuels.

    The EU indicates it cannot accept a deal that 'greenwashes fossil fuels'.

    Oil and gas consumption remains a major flashpoint amid soaring energy prices and tensions over the US-Israeli war with Iran.

    UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres mentioned he was 'deeply disappointed' by the outcome.

    These are the major developments from the closing phase of the UN's COP31 Climate Summit in Antalya, Turkey, on Friday, November 20 through Sunday, November 22:.

    The EU's outright rejection to provide new finance commitments "set the tone" for the failed COP 31 climate summit, says Tasneem Essop, executive director at the Climate Action Network, a group over 2,500 NGOs from various parts of the world.

    Talking to DW from Turkey, Essop questioned the EU's narrative of rejecting the proposed agreement for not mentioning fossil fuels.

    Essop mentioned that the EU was pushing back and obstructing discussions dealing with the issues of the Global South.

    "Rich nations are responsible for providing public finance to developing countries so that they can take climate action, so that they can transition away from fossil fuels," Essop stated.

    It has been revealed that "That requires financial support. And yet they came here without finance. So, it's left a bitter taste in many mouths about the action of rejection by the EU.".

    Essop also pointed to the UK, Australia, and European countries granting additional licenses to obtain fossil fuels.

    "You can't say you're rejecting something because of fossil fuels and yet in your practice and your actions back home, you're doing exactly the opposite," she noted.

    She described the outcome of the summit, which went into overtime and then ended without an agreement, as "deeply disappointing.".

    While oil producers like Saudi Arabia and Russia were criticized for blocking any mention fossil fuels in the draft COP31 declaration, one climate campaigner told DW that other wealthy countries also failed more vulnerable nations by not agreeing to a funded pathway for an energy transition.

    Harjit Sing, strategic advisor to the Fossil Fuel Non-Proliferation Treaty Initiative said developing nations had major ambitions to turn away from oil and gas, but needed resources to do so.

    "If you look at Canada, the UK, Norway, not to mention the US, they continue to expand fossil fuels, yet they point fingers towards developing countries who have a large population," Sing told DW.

    "But the reality is that [the developed countries] were the ones who were blocking the conversation and the progress that we needed to create a just transition mechanism.".

    Sing remarked this lack of a funded plan for developing countries was more urgent than whether or not the final declaration mentioned fossil fuels.

    Recent findings suggest that "So not mentioning fossil fuels is just one part of it. The more notable thing is we now need a plan, not repackaged national roadmaps, but a fair, fast and funded transition away from fossil fuels," he mentioned.

    Sources indicate that "Fair: So rich countries move fast, [but] they are the ones who are historically responsible for the climate crisis. Fast, which is in line with science. And funded, so that developing countries get the right kind of support to make that shift.".

    A combination of climate change effects and insufficient funding would be "a life or death scenario" for developing countries, Sing added.

    "Even at one degree temperature rise, they were facing so many disasters and we are already going to breach that 1.5 degrees Celsius of warming," he said.

    After the failure of the COP31 summit over fossil fuels, Russia's delegate Sergey Kononuchenko argued that reducing the supply of oil without reducing the demand will cause "deficit, price shock and a switch to dirtier types of fuel" as well as "energy poverty," which will affect poorer countries first.

    "For that reason, we cannot agree to any formulation on fossil fuel," he remarked.

    Meanwhile, Saudi Arabia's representative referred to a last-minute proposal that called for expanding carbon capture capacities.

    "We believe that climate change requires all solutions on the table," stated Mohammad Ayoub, speaking for the Arab Group of nations at the summit.

    Recent findings suggest that "It makes no sense that solutions, concrete solutions... will be taken off the table.".

    While capturing carbon dioxide from the atmosphere is technically possible, critics say the technology is still in its infancy and lacks real-world infrastructure to move the needle on climate change.

    Both Russia and Saudi Arabia had sought to omit any mention of fossil fuels in the final declaration, contributing the the impasse on Sunday.

    UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres stated he was "deeply disappointed" by the collapse of negotiations for a joint resolution at COP31.

    "I share the very profound frustration of all those who expected governments to rise to the moment the climate crisis demands," Guterres remarked in a statement.

    "There may be no consensus in the negotiating room. There is no ambiguity in the science," he added.

    According to recent reports, "Those who profit from the destruction of our planet must never dictate the terms of the fight to save it," the UN chief said. "The continued addiction to coal, oil and gas is fueling climate chaos, exposing economies to price shocks, and undermining energy security," Guterres added.

    "Major emitters must lead. Developed countries must deliver on finance. And every country must do their part.".

    Marshall Islands climate envoy Kathy Jetnil-Kijiner spoke out against fossil fuel interests after the conclusion of the summit with no deal.

    It has been revealed that the Marshall Islands are a chain of volcanic atolls and coral islands numbering over 1,100 islands in total in the Pacific Ocean. Like many island nations, they are severly threatened by the effects of climate change on the earth's oceans.

    Industry observers note that "We have been let down ​on all sides. We were presented with the worst possible response to overshoot, a ⁠response to enhance oil and gas. We will not be forced to accept false solutions," Jetnil-Kijiner stated.

    Sources indicate that "We will not compromise our future to benefit fossil fuel interests. We will not accept an outcome that undermines our security and threatens our future.".

    Australian environment minister and COP31's president of negotiations, Chris Bowen, expressed disappointment that the sweeping deal he tried to broker ultimately collapsed.

    As part of a compromise between the two countries, Turkey hosted the summit while Australia took a leading role over negotiations.

    "Unfortunately, we were unable to reach agreement on a cover decision... And that's disappointing. Very disappointing," remarked Bowen.

    "An obvious matter is the transition away from fossil fuels, where some parties insisted that must be mentioned, other parties insisted that if it was mentioned they would veto.".

    Nevertheless, Bowen highlighted some of the ways in which the summit has still had a positive impact.

    "A lot of good things happened this COP. A lot of events which told the clean energy story. A lot of commitments made — like the more than 90 countries that signed the electrification pledge, for example. And all that is good work and a great thing," he said.

    The COP31 climate summit has failed to agree on a final joint declaration.

    During a plenary session, the summit's Turkish president acknowledged there would be no climate deal.

    It has been revealed that "I understand that there is no agreement on this text. For that reason, these decisions have not been adopted," Murat Kurum, who is also Turkey's environment minister, told a closing plenary in the Mediterranean city of Antalya.

    The rift centered on whether to include the phaseout of fossil fuels in the final declaration. Scientists say the burning of fossil fuels such as coal, oil and gas is the main cause of global warming.

    European nations, smaller island states and climate activists have criticized oil-producing countries for the omission.

    Several nations continued to raise serious objections to the draft.

    Antwi-Boasiako Amoah, chair of the African Group of Negotiators, took a shot at the presidency for how it has handled the negotiations.

    In a recent development, "With all due respect Mr. President, you have not shown respect to a group of 54 countries (from Africa) and my country (Ghana) for that matter," Amoah said.

    Panama's representative said the Central American nation was amongst those who suffer most from the consequences and matter of climate justice.

    Panamanian Environment Minister Juan Carlos Navarro stated the talks were being held hostage by a "petroleum mafia" and need to be reformed.

    He mentioned science must be the basis for the cover decision, adding that those who contributed to this crisis must shoulder the responsibility to deal with it.

    According to recent reports, "We are running out of time," Navarro told attendees. "Panama cannot support this decision. The planet cannot continue to wait.".

    Ireland's Climate Minister Darragh O'Brien has said the European Union is "profoundly disappointed" with the current draft deal on the table at COP31 because it "fails to meet the moment" and that the bloc will not agree to it.

    "We will not endorse a cover decision that does not respond to the science, that disregards the implementation gap, and risks deepening the chasm between global commitments and the action required to correct the overshoot and bring 1.5°C within reach," O'Brien stated.

    Sources indicate that "We will not endorse a cover decision that does not even mention fossil fuels, the driver of climate change. And we will not accept negotiating backward in time. And we will not accept a COP that greenwashes fossil fuels," he added.

    Former Greenpeace executive Jennifer Morgan noted it would be better to end the COP31 summit with no deal than a watered-down declaration.

    Her remarks come amid deep divisions over the omission of fossil fuels from the draft declaration.

    Morgan rejected the notion that it would be better to accept the current draft than have no resolution at all, as the Turkish COP president has suggested.

    "I think this is the day for the first time in my 31 COPs that I thought it was better not to have a decision that sets us back, that goes against what small islands and vulnerable people are saying," Morgan added.

    She praised Germany for standing up to pressures to accept the current deal.

    "Of course it would have been better to have a strong outcome here with everyone moving forward, but I agree with the German minister who just said if the text stays the way that it is, then it should not be accepted," Morgan said.

    The US climate activist blamed oil-producing nations for the impasse.

    "Saudi Arabia's fingerprints are all over" the current draft proposal, she noted.

    The omission has created a deadlock at COP31, which was due to conclude on Friday but has been extended as delegates seek consensus.

    Morgan also blamed this year's Turkish presidency for failing to bring everybody together and instead letting countries that rely on fossil fuels dictate the terms of the agreement.

    Recent findings suggest that "Last year we had Brazil with a very strong presidency. They worked all year to bring countries together and they managed. It was not easy last year," Morgan remarked.

    "This year we had presidencies that, in my view, were not well prepared. They did not bring countries together  (...) it's been shuttle diplomacy with no text for four days. That's not the way you get an agreement here," she added.

    German Environment Minister Carsten Schneider has noted the latest version of the draft agreement is "not acceptable.".

    Schneider said that the draft decision "not only fails to provide an adequate response but actually takes a step backward. A step backward from previous decisions on climate protection is the last thing Germany can support.".

    Schneider remarked that delegates had been working hard for days to reach a unanimous decision on "the world's greatest challenge: human-induced climate change," noting that this summer had "shown that the nature of this warming not only costs lives — as in Nepal — but also changes our world for the worse.".

    "It is up to us, as humanity, to do something about it. That is why a conference dedicated to climate protection — whose sole purpose is to protect the climate — must send a clear signal that we are taking action against this threat.".

    Schneider stated he still believed most nations are willing to work to enact climate protection, but singled out those who still rely on fossil fuels to power their economies.

    "The overwhelming majority of nations are committed to climate protection. Some, however, are still making huge profits from oil and gas and are unwilling to scale back their production or to pioneer a clear roadmap for reducing greenhouse gas emissions in this area," he added.

    France has called a fresh draft deal proposed at COP31 a "backward" step.

    French Ecological Transition Minister Monique Barbut criticized the deal for failing to mention fossil fuels, casting fresh uncertainty over whether nations will be able to reach an agreement.

    "Time is ticking and we are not there yet," French Ecological Transition Minister Monique Barbut said in a statement.

    COP31 President Murat Kurum has expressed his frustration over the deadlock at the summit.

    The latest version of the draft deal again fails to mention fossil fuels, the main cause of global warming.

    Over 40 hours after its scheduled conclusion and with no compromise in sight, the summit risks losing the numbers required to make any decision as delegates leave for home.

    "If it is not adopted, I believe those who push the COP process into a deadlock will need to reflect on their position," Kurum stated.

    "It is our wish that this resolution be passed. We shall shortly be expressing our determination to ensure that this resolution is passed at the general meeting," he stated.

    "It is up to the parties involved. If there is sincerity here, and if there is a genuine desire to get things done, I believe that this can be achieved in this chamber. We shall see about that in a moment," Kurum added.

    The third draft makes no mention of the words  "fossil," "oil," "coal," or "phase out.".

    However, as in the second draft, the latest version retains a goal to boost electricity's share of global energy use to 35% by 2035, as well as efforts to expand the use of "clean energy.".

    The draft text also does not stipulate that the "35-by-35" electrification target should be met using renewable energy sources.

    It also urges countries to "accelerate" carbon capture and storage — a controversial technology backed by the fossil fuel industry.

    #58780. The drawbacks of adding solar panels to your home

    📅 22 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1069 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Engadget ↗ Open Full Page

    The drawbacks of adding solar panels to your home

    📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1069 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Engadget

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • On the surface, adding solar panels to your home seems like a fantastic idea.
    • It has been revealed that with all that in mind, why wouldn't you want to add solar panels to your home?
    • The average price to install a solar power system in a typical home falls between $20,000 and $27,000, with a national benchmark of $3.36 per watt, before any incentives or rebates are applied.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    On the surface, adding solar panels to your home seems like a fantastic idea. They can cut down your monthly electricity bills, potentially increase the resale value of your home and deliver clean, renewable and environmentally friendly energy to your residence. Some states and utility companies even provide solar incentives to homeowners in the form of rebates and income tax credits.

    It has been revealed that with all that in mind, why wouldn't you want to add solar panels to your home? Well, for all the good they can do, solar panels also come with plenty of drawbacks, especially if you don't live in a state with solar-friendly regulations, your home isn't geographically positioned to take full advantage of solar energy or your electricity bill isn't all that high to begin with.

    The average price to install a solar power system in a typical home falls between $20,000 and $27,000, with a national benchmark of $3.36 per watt, before any incentives or rebates are applied. Prior to 2026, homeowners could rely on a federal 30 percent tax credit to soften the blow, but the Trump administration terminated that incentive.

    In a recent development, the upfront expense might not be worth the investment, depending on a few factors. First, consider your electricity rate and usage. Some areas charge more for electricity than others, with the 10 most expensive states being Hawaii, Maine, Massachusetts, California, Alaska, Fresh York, Rhode Island, New Hampshire, New Jersey and Connecticut.

    If you don't reside in one of those states, installing solar power may not significantly impact your electricity bill, especially if you live in a smaller home, have a small household (people-wise), use energy-efficient appliances and tend not to consume much energy in a given month.

    According to recent reports, you should also research whether your utility company offers net metering or other incentives and rebates. Net metering gives homeowners credits for any excess energy produced by their solar panels, allowing you to reduce or even potentially erase a monthly electric bill. This incentive is not available everywhere, and the programs differ by state.

    For example, the most advantageous programs for solar panel users offer a one-to-one power exchange that credits you at the same retail rate you pay for your power. Other states utilize buyback programs or reduced-rate or net billing structures that credit homeowners a portion of what they pay for energy.

    Sources indicate that some geographic locations are simply better than others when it comes to solar panels. Places with consistent sunlight and moderate-to-cool temperatures are best. An abundance of overcast weather or excessive heat can negatively impact panel performance and life.

    The design of your house also needs to be considered. Solar panels are almost always installed on roofs that face south and are clear of buildings, trees or other objects that may block sunlight. If your roof is on the older side, solar panels aren't ideal unless you have a newly introduced roof installed, and that can cost anywhere from $4,000 to more than $35,000 depending on the size of your home and the type of roof.

    Then there are simple aesthetics. Some homeowners, especially those who just paid for a brand new roof, don't want to cover it up with bulky and — let's face it — unattractive solar panels. Solar shingles are an alternative option, but they've attracted some negative press and also cost roughly twice the price per watt as standard solar panels. At $21 to $25 per square foot installed, the price to install solar shingles on a 2,500-square-foot home comes to between $52,500 and $62,500 before incentives.

    It has been revealed that aside from lowering monthly electric bills and moving toward clean energy, having backup power during blackouts is a major appeal for homeowners looking to switch to solar, but it's not as simple as many people think. When your home loses power, solar energy doesn't just kick into gear. It requires a battery backup system that stores excess solar energy from the panels, then delivers it to your home when the power is out. And — you guessed it — it's expensive.

    Sources indicate that for a single-battery backup system, which is enough to power the average home's lights, refrigerator, WiFi and some power outlets during outages, you're looking at spending between $10,000 and $16,000. If you want a whole-home, multi-battery backup, which can power your home's HVAC system and all appliances, that price range escalates to $22,000 to $40,000, plus routine maintenance costs.

    That all combines to drastically increase your solar investment and potentially extend the payback period, which can lead to major problems if you decide you want to move before the system is paid off.

    Solar panels can add resale value to your home, but there's a major caveat to consider: If you haven't fully paid off the cost of your home's solar equipment, prospective homebuyers may view that as a negative.

    Why? Because if you opted to finance the installation cost or entered into a power purchase agreement (PPA) with your utility manufacturer, the buyer must agree to assume the remainder of the contract. If the buyer refuses to take over the contract, the most straightforward solution is to pay off the balance. Unfortunately, that's also the most expensive solution.

    Here's another drawback: whoever buys your home must also qualify for the lease on the solar equipment. Being approved for a mortgage is separate from being approved for a solar lease, so if the buyer isn't approved for the solar lease, the entire home sale could fall apart. Plus, the lease-approval process can take up to two months, so this would need to be taken care of well ahead of closing.

    Then there's the UCC-1, which is essentially a lien against the solar equipment filed by most solar leasing companies with local land registries. Because the UCC-1 turns up in property title searches, this can turn into a huge problem if the buyer's mortgage lender refuses to close the transaction because of this open, pending matter. And it does happen because the bank providing the mortgage loan does not want to have a solar organization standing in front of them should the house need to be seized and sold by the lender to recoup its money. Lenders can, and do, often refuse to provide the buyer with the loan as long as the UCC-1 remains active.
